47.e: O foolish beast! Thou doth not recognize Him, Whose Glory hath spread over all the three worlds.

47.g: ਪੂਜਤ ਹੈ ਪਰਮੇਸਰ ਕੈ ਜਿਹ ਕੇ ਪਰਸੈ ਪਰਲੋਕ ਪਰਾਹੀ ॥
47.t: poojat hai paramesar kai jeh ke parasai paralok paraahee ||
47.e: Thou worshippest those as God, by whose touch thou shalt be driven far away from the next world.

47.g: ਪਾਪ ਕਰੋ ਪਰਮਾਰਥ ਕੈ ਜਿਹ ਪਾਪਨ ਤੇ ਅਤਿ ਪਾਪ ਲਜਾਈ ॥
47.t: paap karo paramaarath kai jeh paapan te at paap lajaiee ||
47.e: Thou art committing such sins in th name of parmarath (the subtle truth) that by committing them the Great sins may feel shy.

47.g: ਪਾਇ ਪਰੋ ਪਰਮੇਸਰ ਕੇ ਜੜ ਪਾਹਨ ਮੈਂ ਪਰਮੇਸਰ ਨਾਹੀ ॥੯੯॥
47.t: pai paro paramesar ke jaR paahan mai(n) paramesar naahee ||99||
47.e: O fool! Fall at the feet of Lord-God, the Lord is not within the stone-idols.99.

47.g: ਮੋਨ ਭਜੇ ਨਹੀ ਮਾਨ ਤਜੇ ਨਹੀ ਭੇਖ ਸਜੇ ਨਹੀ ਮੂੰਡ ਮੁੰਡਾਏ ॥
47.t: mon bhaje nahee maan taje nahee bhekh saje nahee moo(n)dd mu(n)ddaae ||
47.e: The Lord cannot be realized by observing silence, by forsaking pride, by adopting guises and by shaving the head.

47.g: ਕੰਠ ਨ ਕੰਠੀ ਕਠੋਰ ਧਰੇ ਨਹੀ ਸੀਸ ਜਟਾਨ ਕੇ ਜੂਟ ਸੁਹਾਏ ॥
47.t: ka(n)Th na ka(n)Thee kaThor dhare nahee sees jaTaan ke jooT suhaae ||
47.e: He cannot be realized by wearing Kanthi (a short necklace of small beads of different kinds made of wood or seeds worn by mendicants or ascetics) for severe austerities or Thy making a knot of matted hair on the head.

47.g: ਸਾਚੁ ਕਹੋਂ ਸੁਨ ਲੈ ਚਿਤ ਦੈ ਬਿਨੁ ਦੀਨ ਦਿਆਲ ਕੀ ਸਾਮ ਸਿਧਾਏ ॥
47.t: saach kaho(n) sun lai chit dhai bin dheen dhiaal kee saam sidhaae ||
47.e: Listen attentively, I speak Turth, Thou shalt not achieve the target without going under the Refuge of the LORD, Who is ever Merciful to the lowly.

47.g: ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਕਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਯਤ ਹੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾਲ ਨ ਭੀਜਤ ਲਾਂਡ ਕਟਾਏ ॥੧੦੦॥
47.t: preet kare prabh paayat hai kirapaal na bheejat laa(n)dd kaTaae ||100||
47.e: God can only be realized with LOVE, He is not pleased by circumcision.100.

47.g: ਕਾਗਦ ਦੀਪ ਸਭੈ ਕਰਿ ਕੈ ਅਰੁ ਸਾਤ ਸਮੁੰਦ੍ਰਨ ਕੀ ਮਸੁ ਕੈ ਹੋਂ ॥
47.t: kaagadh dheep sabhai kar kai ar saat samu(n)dhran kee mas kai ho(n) ||
47.e: If all the continents are transformed into paper and all the seven seas into ink

47.g: ਕਾਟ ਬਨਾਸਪਤੀ ਸਗਰੀ ਲਿਖਬੇ ਹੂੰ ਕੇ ਲੇਖਨ ਕਾਜਿ ਬਨੈ ਹੋਂ ॥
47.t: kaaT banaasapatee sagaree likhabe hoo(n) ke lekhan kaaj banai ho(n) ||
47.e: By chopping all the vegetation the pen may be made for the sake of writing

47.g: ਸਾਰਸੁਤੀ ਬਕਤਾ ਕਰਿ ਕੈ ਜੁਗਿ ਕੋਟਿ ਗਨੇਸ ਕੈ ਹਾਥਿ ਲਿਖੈ ਹੋਂ ॥
47.t: saarasutee bakataa kar kai jug koT ganes kai haath likhai ho(n) ||
47.e: If the goddess Saraswati be made the speaker (of eulogies) and Ganesha be there to write with hands for millions of ages

47.g: ਕਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾਨ ਬਿਨਾ ਬਿਨਤੀ ਨ ਤਊ ਤੁਮ ਕੌ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਨੈਕ ਰਿਝੈ ਹੋਂ ॥੧੦੧॥
47.t: kaal kirapaan binaa binatee na tuoo tum kau prabh naik rijhai ho(n) ||101||
47.e: Even then, O God! O sword-incannate KAL! Without supplication, none can make Thee pleased even a little.101.

47.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਕਾਲ ਜੀ ਕੀ ਉਸਤਤਿ ਪ੍ਰਿਥਮ ਧਿਆਏ ਸੰਪੂਰਨ ਸੁਭ ਮਸਤੁ ॥੧॥ਅਫਜੂ॥
47.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the sree kaal jee kee usatat piratham dhiaae sa(n)pooran subh masat ||1||afajoo||
47.e: Here ends the First Chapter of BACHITTAR NATAK entitled The Eulogy of Sri KAL.’1.
AUTOBIOGRAPHY
CHAUPAI
O Lord! Thy Praise is Supreme and Infinite,

47.g: ਜਾ ਕਾ ਲਹਿਓ ਨ ਕਿਨਹੂੰ ਪਾਰਾ ॥
47.t: jaa kaa lahio na kinahoo(n) paaraa ||
47.e: None could comprehend its limits.
O God of gods and King of kings,
The Merciful Lord of the lowly and protector of the humble.1.
DOHRA

47.g: ਮੂਕ ਉਚਰੈ ਸਾਸਤ੍ਰ ਖਟ ਪਿੰਗੁ ਗਿਰਨ ਚੜਿ ਜਾਇ ॥
47.t: mook ucharai saasatr khaT pi(n)g giran chaR jai ||
47.e: The dumb utters the six Shastras and  the crippled climbs the mountain.

47.g: ਅੰਧ ਲਖੈ ਬਧਰੋ ਸੁਨੈ ਜੌ ਕਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਾਇ ॥੨॥
47.t: a(n)dh lakhai badharo sunai jau kaal kirapaa karai ||2||
47.e: The blind one sees and the deaf listens, if the KAL becomes Gracious.2.
CHAUPAI
O God! My intellect is trifling.
How can it narrate Thy Praise?

47.g: ਹਮ ਨ ਸਕਤ ਕਰ ਸਿਫਤ ਤੁਮਾਰੀ ॥
47.t: ham na sakat kar sifat tumaaree ||
47.e: I cannot (have sufficient words to) praise Thee,
Thou mayst Thyself improve this narration.3.
Upto what limit this insect can depict (Thy Praises)?
Thou mayst Thyself improve Thy Greatness.

47.g: ਪਿਤਾ ਜਨਮ ਜਿਮ ਪੂਤ ਨ ਪਾਵੈ ॥
47.t: pitaa janam jim poot na paavai ||
47.e: Just as the son cannot say anything about the birth of his father
Then how can one unfold Thy mystery.4.
Thy Greatness is Only Thine
It cannot be described by others.

47.g: ਤੁਮਰੀ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਤੁਮ ਹੰੂ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਜਾਨੋ ॥
47.t: tumaree kirapaa tum ha(n)oo prabh jaano ||
47.e: O Lord! Only Thou knowest Thy doings.
Who hast the power to elucidate Thy High of Low acts? 5.
Thou hast made one thousand hoods of Sheshanaga
Which contain two thousand tongues.
He is reciting till now Thy Infinite Names
Even then he hath not know the end of Thy Names.6.
What can one say about Thy doings?
One gets puzzled while understanding it.
Thy subtle form is indescribable
(Therefore) I speak about Thy Immanent Form.7.
When I shall observe Thy loving Devotion

47.g: ਛੋਰ ਕਥਾ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਤਬ ਕਹਿਹੌ ॥
47.t: chhor kathaa sabh hee tab kahihau ||
47.e: I shall then describe all Thy anecdotes from the beginning.

47.g: ਅਬ ਮੈ ਕਹੋ ਸੁ ਅਪਨੀ ਕਥਾ ॥
47.t: ab mai kaho su apanee kathaa ||
47.e: Now I narrate my own life-story
How the Sodhi clan came into being (in this world).8.
DOHRA

47.g: ਪ੍ਰਿਥਮ ਕਥਾ ਸੰਛੇਪ ਤੇ ਕਹੋ ਸੁ ਹਿਤੁ ਚਿਤੁ ਲਾਇ ॥
47.t: piratham kathaa sa(n)chhep te kaho su hit chit lai ||
47.e: With the concentration of my mind, I narrate in brief my earlier story.

47.g: ਬਹੁਰ ਬਡੋ ਬਿਸਥਾਰ ਕੈ ਕਹਿਹੌ ਸਭੋ ਸੁਨਾਇ ॥੯॥
47.t: bahur baddo bisathaar kai kahihau sabho sunai ||9||
47.e: Then after that, I shall relate all in great detail.9.
CHAUPAI
In the beginning when KAL created the world
It was brought into being by Aumkara (the One Lord).
Kal sain was the first king
Who was of immeasurable strength and supreme beauty.10.
Kalket became the second king
And Kurabaras, the third.
Kaldhuj was the fourth kin

47.g: ਜਿਹ ਤੇ ਭਇਓ ਜਗਤ ਸਭ ਕੋ ਹੈ ॥੧੧॥
47.t: jeh te bhio jagat sabh ko hai ||11||
47.e: From whom the whole world originated. 11.

47.g: ਸਹਸ ਪਾਦ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਤਨ ਮੋ ਹੈਂ ॥
47.t: sahas paadh jaa ke tan mo hai(n) ||
47.e: He had a thousand eyes and thousand feet.
He slept on Sheshanaga
Therefore he was called the master of Shesha.12.
Out of the secretion from one of his ears

47.g: ਤਾ ਤੇ ਮਧੁ ਕੀਟਭ ਤਨ ਧਾਰਾ ॥
47.t: taa te madh keeTabh tan dhaaraa ||
47.e: Madhu and Kaitabh came into being.

48.e: And from the secretion of the other ear

48.g: ਤਾ ਤੇ ਭਈ ਸ੍ਰਿਸਟਿ ਇਹ ਸਾਰੀ ॥੧੩॥
48.t: taa te bhiee sirasaT ieh saaree ||13||
48.e: The whole world materialized.13.

48.g: ਤਿਨ ਕੋ ਕਾਲ ਬਹੁਰ ਬਧ ਕਰਾ ॥
48.t: tin ko kaal bahur badh karaa ||
48.e: After some period the Lord killed the demons (Madhu and Kaitabh).

48.g: ਤਿਨ ਕੋ ਮੇਦ ਸਮੁੰਦ ਮੋ ਪਰਾ ॥
48.t: tin ko medh samu(n)dh mo paraa ||
48.e: Their marrow flowed into the ocean.

48.g: ਚਿਕਨ ਤਾਸ ਜਲ ਪਰ ਤਿਰ ਰਹੀ ॥
48.t: chikan taas jal par tir rahee ||
48.e: The greasy substance floated thereon because of that medital (marrow)
The earth was called medha (or medani).14.
Because of virtuous actions
A purusha (person) is known as devta (god)

48.g: ਕੁਕ੍ਰਿਤ ਕਰਮ ਜੇ ਜਗ ਮੈ ਕਰਹੀਂ ॥
48.t: kukirat karam je jag mai karahee(n) ||
48.e: And because of evil actions

48.g: ਨਾਮ ਅਸੁਰ ਤਿਨ ਕੋ ਸਭ ਧਰਹੀਂ ॥੧੫॥
48.t: naam asur tin ko sabh dharahee(n) ||15||
48.e: He is known as asura (demon).15.
If everything is described in detail

48.g: ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਬਢਨ ਤੇ ਅਤਿ ਡਰੁ ਮਾਨੀਅਤ ॥
48.t: gra(n)th baddan te at ddar maaneeat ||
48.e: It is feared that the description will become voluminous.

48.g: ਤਿਨ ਤੇ ਹੋਤ ਬਹੁਤ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਆਏ ॥
48.t: tin te hot bahut nirap aae ||
48.e: There were many kings after Kaldhuj
Like Daksha Prajapati etc. 16.

48.g: ਦਸ ਸਹੰਸ੍ਰ ਤਿਹਿ ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਭਈ ਕੰਨਿਆ ॥
48.t: dhas saha(n)sr teh gireh bhiee ka(n)niaa ||
48.e: Ten thousand daughters were born to them

48.g: ਜਿਹ ਸਮਾਨ ਕਹ ਲਗੈ ਨ ਅੰਨਿਆ ॥
48.t: jeh samaan keh lagai na a(n)niaa ||
48.e: Whose beauty was not matched by others.
In due course all these daughters
Were married with the kings.17.
DOHRA

48.g: ਬਨਤਾ ਕਦਰੂ ਦਿਤਿ ਅਦਿਤਿ ਏ ਰਿਖ ਬਰੀ ਬਨਾਇ ॥
48.t: banataa kadharoo dhit adhit e rikh baree banai ||
48.e: Banita, Kadaru, Diti and Aditi became the wives of sages (rishis),

48.g: ਨਾਗ ਨਾਗਰਿਪੁ ਦੇਵ ਸਭ ਦਈਤ ਲਏ ਉਪਜਾਇ ॥੧੮॥
48.t: naag naagarip dhev sabh dhieet le upajai ||18||
48.e: And Nagas, their enemies (like Garuda), the gods and demons were born to them.18.
CHAUPAI

48.g: ਤਾ ਤੇ ਸੂਰਜ ਰੂਪ ਕੋ ਧਰਾ ॥
48.t: taa te sooraj roop ko dharaa ||

48.g: ਜਾ ਤੇ ਬੰਸ ਪ੍ਰਚੁਰ ਰਵਿ ਕਰਾ ॥
48.t: jaa te ba(n)s prachur rav karaa ||
48.e: From that (Aditi), the sun was born, from whom Suraj Vansh (the Sun dynasty) originated.

48.g: ਜੋ ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਕਹਿ ਨਾਮ ਸੁਨਾਊ ॥
48.t: jo tin ke keh naam sunaauoo ||

48.e: If I describe the names of the kings of this of this clan, I fear a great extension of the story.19.

48.g: ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਬੰਸ ਬਿਖੈ ਰਘੁ ਭਯੋ ॥
48.t: tin ke ba(n)s bikhai ragh bhayo ||

48.e: In this clan, there was a king named Raghu, who was the originator of Raghuvansh (the clan of Raghu) in the world.

48.g: ਤਾ ਤੇ ਪੁਤ੍ਰ ਹੋਤ ਭਯੋ ਅਜ ਬਰ ॥
48.t: taa te putr hot bhayo aj bar ||

48.g: ਮਹਾ ਰਥੀ ਅਰ ਮਹਾ ਧਨੁਰ ਧਰ ॥੨੦॥
48.t: mahaa rathee ar mahaa dhanur dhar ||20||
48.e: He had a great son Aja, a mighty warrior and superb archer.20.

48.g: ਜਬ ਤਿਨ ਭੇਸ ਜੋਗ ਕੋ ਲਯੋ ॥
48.t: jab tin bhes jog ko layo ||

48.e: When he renounced the world as a Yogi, he passed on his kingdom to his son Dastratha.

48.g: ਹੋਤ ਭਯੋ ਵਹ ਮਹਾ ਧਨੁਰ ਧਰ ॥
48.t: hot bhayo veh mahaa dhanur dhar ||

48.g: ਤੀਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਆਨ ਬਰਾ ਜਿਹ ਰੁਚਿ ਕਰ ॥੨੧॥
48.t: teen triaan baraa jeh ruch kar ||21||
48.e: Who had been a great archer and had married three wives with pleasure.21.
The eldest one gave birth to Rama, the others gave birth to Bharat, Lakshman and Shatrughan.
They ruled over their kingdom for a long time, after which they left for their heavenly abode.22.

48.g: ਸੀਅ ਸੁਤ ਬਹੁਰ ਭਏ ਦੁਇ ਰਾਜਾ ॥
48.t: seea sut bahur bhe dhui raajaa ||

48.e: After that the two sons of Sita (and Rama) became the kings.

48.g: ਭਾਂਤਿ ਭਾਂਤਿ ਕੇ ਜੱਗ ਕੀਏ ਤਬ ॥੨੩॥
48.t: bhaa(n)t bhaa(n)t ke ja'g ke'ee tab ||23||
48.e: They married the Punjabi princesses and performed various types of sacrifices.23.
There they founded two cities, the one Kasur and the other Lahore.
Both the cities surpassed in beauty to that of Lanka and Amravati. 24.
For a long time, both the brothers ruled over their kingdom and ultimately they were bound down by the noose of death.

49.g: ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਪੁੱਤ੍ਰ ਪੌਤ੍ਰ ਜੇ ਵਏ ॥
49.t: tin ke pu'tr pauatr je ve ||

49.g: ਰਾਜ ਕਰਤ ਇਹ ਜਗ ਕੋ ਭਏ ॥੨੫॥
49.t: raaj karat ieh jag ko bhe ||25||
49.e: After them their sons and grandson ruled over the world.25.

49.g: ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਨਾਮ ਨ ਸੰਖ੍ਯਾ ਪਾਊਂ ॥
49.t: tin ke naam na sa(n)khayaa paauoo(n) ||
49.e: They were innumerable, therefore it is difficult to describe all.

49.g: ਹੋਤ ਚਹੂੰ ਜੁਗ ਮੈਂ ਜੇ ਆਏ ॥
49.t: hot chahoo(n) jug mai(n) je aae ||

49.g: ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਨਾਮ ਨ ਜਾਤ ਗਨਾਏ ॥੨੬॥
49.t: tin ke naam na jaat ganaae ||26||
49.e: It is not possible to count the names of all those who ruled over their kingdoms in all the four ages.26.

49.g: ਜੌ ਅਬ ਤਉ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਬਲ ਪਾਊਂ ॥
49.t: jau ab tau kirapaa bal paauoo(n) ||

49.e: If now you shower your grace upon me, I shall describe (a few) names, as I know them.

49.g: ਜਿਨ ਤੇ ਭਏ ਪੁਤ੍ਰ ਘਰ ਅਨਗਨ ॥੨੭॥
49.t: jin te bhe putr ghar anagan ||27||
49.e: Kalket and Kal Rai had innumerable descendants.27.
Kalket was a mighty warrior, who drove out Kal Rai from his city.
Kal Rai settled in the country named Sanaudh and married the king’s daughter.28.

49.g: ਤਿਹ ਤੇ ਪੁਤ੍ਰ ਭਯੋ ਜੋ ਧਾਮਾ ॥
49.t: teh te putr bhayo jo dhaamaa ||

49.e: A son was born to him, who was named Sodhi Rai.

49.g: ਵੰਸ ਸਨੌਢ ਤਾ ਦਿਨ ਤੇ ਥੀਆ ॥
49.t: va(n)s sanauadd taa dhin te theeaa ||

49.e: Sodhi Rai was the founder of Sanaudh dynasty by the Will of the Supreme Purusha.29.

49.g: ਤਾਂ ਤੇ ਪੁਤ੍ਰ ਪੌਤ੍ਰ ਹੋਇ ਆਏ ॥
49.t: taa(n) te putr pauatr hoi aae ||

49.e: His sons and grandsons were called sodhis.

49.g: ਜਗ ਮੈ ਅਧਿਕ ਸੁ ਭਏ ਪ੍ਰਸਿੱਧਾ ॥
49.t: jag mai adhik su bhe prasi'dhaa ||

49.g: ਦਿਨ ਦਿਨ ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਧਨ ਕੀ ਬ੍ਰਿੱਧਾ ॥੩੦॥
49.t: dhin dhin tin ke dhan kee bira'dhaa ||30||
49.e: They became very famous in the world and gradually prospered in wealth.30.
They ruled over the country in various ways and subdued kings of many countries.
They extended their Dharma everywhere and had the royal canopy over their head.31.
They performed Rajasu sacrifice several times declaring themselves as supreme rulers, after conquering kings of various countries.

49.g: ਸਕਲ ਕਲੂਖ ਨਿਜ ਕੁਲ ਕੇ ਹਰੇ ॥੩੨॥
49.t: sakal kalookh nij kul ke hare ||32||
49.e: They performed Bajmedh-sacrifice (horse—sacrifice) several times, clearing their dynasty of all the blemishes.32.

49.g: ਮੇਟ ਨ ਸਕਾ ਕੋਊ ਤਿਹ ਸਾਧਾ ॥
49.t: meT na sakaa kouoo teh saadhaa ||
49.e: After that there arose quarrels and differences within the dynasty, and none could set the things right.

49.g: ਗਹਿ ਗਹਿ ਚਲੇ ਭਿਰਨ ਰਨ ਮੰਡਲ ॥੩੩॥
49.t: geh geh chale bhiran ran ma(n)ddal ||33||
49.e: The great warriors and archers moved towards the battlefield for a fight.33.

49.g: ਜਿਨ ਕਾ ਮੂਆ ਕਰਤ ਜਗ ਘੇਰਾ ॥
49.t: jin kaa mooaa karat jag gheraa ||
49.e: The world hath perished after quarrel on wealth and property from very olden times.
The attachment, ego and infights spread widely and the world was conquered by lust and anger.34.
DOHRA

49.g: ਧੰਨਿ ਧੰਨਿ ਧਨ ਕੋ ਭਾਖੀਐ ਜਾ ਕਾ ਜਗਤੁ ਗੁਲਾਮੁ ॥
49.t: dha(n)n dha(n)n dhan ko bhaakheeaai jaa kaa jagat gulaam ||
49.e: The mammon may hailed, who hath the whole world as her slave.

49.g: ਸਭ ਨਿਰਖਤ ਯਾ ਕੌ ਫਿਰੈ ਸਭ ਚਲ ਕਰਤ ਸਲਾਮ ॥੩੫॥
49.t: sabh nirakhat yaa kau firai sabh chal karat salaam ||35||
49.e: All the world goes in search for her and all go to salute her.35.
CHAUPAI.
None could remember KAL and there was only extension of enmity, strife ego.

49.g: ਲੋਭ ਮੂਲ ਇਹਿ ਜਗ ਕੋ ਹੂਆ ॥
49.t: lobh mool ieh jag ko hooaa ||

49.g: ਜਾ ਸੋ ਚਾਹਤ ਸਭੈ ਕੋ ਮੂਆ ॥੩੬॥
49.t: jaa so chaahat sabhai ko mooaa ||36||
49.e: Only greed become the base of the world, because of which everyone wants the other to die.36.

49.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਸੁਭ ਬੰਸ ਬਰਨਨੰ ਨਾਮ ਦੁਤੀਆ ਧਿਆਇ ਸਮਾਪਤ ਮਸਤੁ ਸੁਭ ਮਸਤੁ ॥੨॥ਅਫਜੂ॥੧੩੭॥
49.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the subh ba(n)s baranana(n) naam dhuteeaa dhiaai samaapat masat subh masat ||2||afajoo||137||
49.e: End of the Second Chapter of BACHITTAR NATAK entitled ‘The Description of Ancestry’.2.
BHUJJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

50.g: ਜਿਸੈ ਸਾਧ ਸਾਕਿਓ ਨ ਕੋਊ ਸੁਧਾਰੰ ॥
50.t: jisai saadh saakio na kouoo sudhaara(n) ||
50.e: The Providence created the great vices of enmity and strife, which could not be controlled by any reformer.

50.g: ਗਯੋ ਕਉਨ ਬੀਰੰ ਸੁ ਯਾ ਤੇ ਅਲੋਹੰ ॥੧॥
50.t: gayo kaun beera(n) su yaa te aloha(n) ||1||
50.e: Which warrior could save himself from the blwos of mighty king lust and the great courtiers creed and attachment? 1.

50.g: ਤਹਾਂ ਬੀਰ ਬੰਕੇ ਬਕੈ ਆਪ ਮੱਧੰ ॥
50.t: tahaa(n) beer ba(n)ke bakai aap ma'dha(n) ||

50.g: ਉਠੇ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਲੈ ਲੈ ਮਚਾ ਜੁੱਧ ਸੱੁਧੰ ॥
50.t: auThe sasatr lai lai machaa ju'dh sa'udha(n) ||
50.e: There the youthful warriors are busy challenging shuts amongst themselves, they stand up with their weapons and are engaged in tough fight.
In this fight, somewhere there are innumerable shafts, helmets and double-edged swords in use. The evil spirits and ghosts are dancing and the tabors are resounding.2.

50.g: ਕਹੂੰ ਈਸ ਸੀਸੰ ਪੁਐ ਰੁੰਡ ਮਾਲੰ ॥
50.t: kahoo(n) iees seesa(n) puaai ru(n)dd maala(n) ||

50.e: Somewhere the god Shiva is stringing the skulls in his rosary of skulls, somewhere the vampires and ghosts are shrieking joyfully.

50.g: ਗੁਥੀ ਲੁੱਥ ਜੱੁਥੇ ਬਹੇ ਬੀਰ ਬੰਕੰ ॥੩॥
50.t: guthee lu'th ja'uthe bahe beer ba(n)ka(n) ||3||
50.e: Somewhere the terrible goddess Chamunda is shouting and somewhere the vultures are shrieking. Somewhere the corpses of youthful warriors are lying inter-lovked.3.

50.g: ਪਰੀ ਕੱੁਟ ਕੱੁਟੰ ਰੁਲੇ ਤੱਛ ਮੱੁਛੰ ॥
50.t: paree ka'uT ka'uTa(n) rule ta'chh ma'uchha(n) ||

50.g: ਰਹੇ ਹਾਥ ਡਾਰੇ ਉਭੈ ਉਰਧ ਮੱੁਛੰ ॥
50.t: rahe haath ddaare ubhai uradh ma'uchha(n) ||
50.e: There had been tough battle, because of which the chopped corpses are rolling in dush. Somewhere the dead warriors are lying uncared with their hands on their whiskers.
Somewhere the skulls, helmets, bows and arrows are lying scattered. Somewhere the swords and quivers of the warriors are there in the battlefield.4.
Somewhere the vultures shriek and somewhere the vampire is belching.
Somewhere the evil spirits and ghosts are walking slantingly, somewhere the ghosts, fiends and meateaters are laughing.5.
RASAAVAL STANZA
Hearing the thunder of mighty warriors, the clouds felt shy.
Strong banners have been fixed and highly infuriated the heroes are enaged in war.6.
Holding their swords and daggers, they are fighting in great anger.
The winsome great heroes, with their fighting, make the earth tremble.7.
The warriors are fighting with their weapons in great excitement, the weapons as well as the armour are glistening.
There is the great steel-killing with weapons like swords and daggers.8.
Various types of swords, the swords from Halab and Junab, Sarohi swords and the double-deged sword, knife, spear and dagger were struck with great ire.

50.g: ਕਹੂੰ ਸੇਲ ਸਾਂਗੰ ਭਈ ਰੇਲ ਪੇਲੰ ॥੯॥
50.t: kahoo(n) sel saa(n)ga(n) bhiee rel pela(n) ||9||
50.e: Somewhere the lancet and somewhere the pike only were used, somewhere the lance and the dagger were being used violently.9.
NARAAJ STANZA
The warriors are fiercely adorned with weapons, with which tthey fight forsaking all doubts.
Without hesitation they strike the weapons and chop the limbs.10.
They do not care at all and shout “kill, kill”.
They challenge and drive with force and endure the blows of many weapons.11.
Thousand of houris (beautiful heavenly damsels) move in the sky; they move forward to marry the martyrs.
The warriors move in the battlefield in a frightful manner, and utter “kill, kill” 12.
The limbs of some warrior have been chopped and the hair of some have been uprooted.
The flesh of someone has been peeled and someone hath fallen after being chopped.13.
There is knocking sound of drums and shield. The frontline army hath been uprooted.
The warriors strike their weapons very quickly and trample over the heroic army.14.
New trumpets resound and the mighty warriors with quality of forbearance, roar.
They strike the swords and shoot the arrows and suddenly chop away the limbs. 15.
Filled with anger, they move forward and do not go back even four feet.
They hold the weapons and challenge and hearing their thunder, the clouds feel shy.16.
They raise their heart-rending shouts and strike their weapons violently.
They fight, forgetting all sorrows and several of them move towards heaven.17.

51.e: The warriors filled with ire and moving forward shoot a volley of arrows.
The conch is blown and in such a terrible time, the warriors get adorned with patience. 18.
RASAAVAL STANZA
The trumpet and conch resound and the great warriors look impressive.
The swift-running horses dance and the brave warriors are excited.19.
The glistening sharp swords flash like lightning.
The sound of drums arises and is heard continuously. 20.
Somewhere the double-edged swords and helmets lie broken, somewhere the warriors shout “kill, kill”.
Somewhere the warriors are forcefully knocked about and somewhere, being puzzled, they have fallen down. 21.
The great army is being trampled and limbs are being chopped into halves.
The long steel maces are struck and the shouts of “kill, kill” are raised.22.
The stream of blood is full and the houris walk over the sky.
The goddess Kali is thundering in the sky and the vamps are laughing.23.
The great warriors equipped with steel and filled with ire look impressive.
They roar with great pride and hearing them, the clouds feel shy.24.
The warriors are adorned with steel-weapons and shout “kill, kill”.
They have slanting whiskers on their faces and fight without caring for their life. 25.
There are shouts and the army hath laid the siege.
In great anger the warriors rush from all sides shouting “kill, kill”.26.
The warriors are meeting with their lances like the Ganges with the sea.
Many of them under cover of their shields even break the striking swords with cracking sound.27.
There are shouts after shouts and the swift-running horses dance.
The warriors are highly ferocious and are fighting with the awakening of anger.28.
The sharp lances have fallen down and there is great knocking.
The eaters of flesh are dancing and the warriors are engaged in hot war.29.

52.e: The flesh-eating creatures are laughing and the gangs of ghosts are dancing.
The persistent warriors are moving forward and shouting “kill, kill”.30.
That goddess hath roared in the sky, who hath been brought into being by Supreme KAL.
The ghosts are dancing excitedly and are saturated with great anger.31.
The warriors are fighting with each other because of enmity and the great heroes are falling as martyras.
Fixing their strong banner and with increased enemity they are shouting.32.
They have adorned their head with the ornament and have stretched their bows in their hands.
They shoot their arrows confronting the opponents, some of them fall down, having been chopped into halves.33.
The elephants and horses are lying dead and the warriors engaged in enmity
Fearlessly strike their weapons; both sides wish for their victory.34.
The warriors are roaring and the swiftly-running horses dance.
There are shouts and in this way the army is running about. 35.
The warriors are intoxicated with wine and are absorbed in great rage.
The group of elephants are adorned and the warriors are fighting with increased anger. 36.
The sharp swords glisten like the flash of lightning in the clouds.
The blows are struck on the enemy like the swift-moving water-insect.37.
They strike weapons confronting each other; both sides wish for their victory.
They are absorbed in violent rage and are highly intoxicated.38.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA
The warriors fighting with warriors are looking wonderfully frightening. The clattering sound of kettledrums is heard and there is also the thunder of trumpets.

52.g: ਫਿਰੈ ਰੁੰਡ ਮੁੰਡੰ ਤਨੰ ਤੱਛ ਤੀਰੰ ॥੩੯॥
52.t: firai ru(n)dd mu(n)dda(n) tana(n) ta'chh teera(n) ||39||
52.e: The serious tone of the new trumpets resounds. Somewhere the trunks, somewhere the heads, somewhere the bodies hewed by arrows are seen moving.39.

52.g: ਰੁਲੇ ਤੱਛ ਮੁੱਛੰ ਮਹਾ ਜੋਧ ਜੰਗੰ ॥
52.t: rule ta'chh mu'chha(n) mahaa jodh ja(n)ga(n) ||
52.e: The warriors strike their swords and care for their arrows in the battlefield. The great heroes, chopped in the war are rolling in dust.

52.g: ਬੰਧੇ ਬੀਰ ਬਾਨਾ ਬਡੇ ਐਠਿ ਵਾਰੇ ॥
52.t: ba(n)dhe beer baanaa badde aaiTh vaare ||

52.e: The greatly proud warriors, having tied their quivers and equipped with armour move in the battlefield like the drunkards.40.

52.g: ਉਠੀ ਕੂਹ ਜੂਹੰ ਸਮਰ ਸਾਰ ਬੱਜਿਯੰ ॥
52.t: auThee kooh jooha(n) samar saar ba'jiya(n) ||

52.g: ਕਿਧੋ ਅੰਤ ਕੇ ਕਾਲ ਕੋ ਮੇਘ ਗੱਜਿਯੰ ॥
52.t: kidho a(n)t ke kaal ko megh ga'jiya(n) ||
52.e: The weapons were struck and there was confusion all around, it seemed that the clouds of doomsday were thundering.

53.g: ਬਜੇ ਲੋਹ ਕ੍ਰੋਹੰ ਮਹਾਂ ਜੰਗ ਮੱਚਿਯੰ ॥੪੧॥
53.t: baje loh kroha(n) mahaa(n) ja(n)g ma'chiya(n) ||41||
53.e: Hearing the cracking sound bows, the warriors of great endurance are becoming cowards. The steel clatters in rage with steel nad the great war is in progress.41.
The youthful warriors are moving in this great war, with naked swords the fighters look wonderfully terrible.

53.g: ਬਲੀ ਜੁੱਝ ਰੱੁਝੈ ਰਸੰ ਰੁਦ੍ਰ ਰੱਤੇ ॥
53.t: balee ju'jh ra'ujhai rasa(n) rudhr ra'te ||

53.g: ਮਿਲੇ ਹੱਥ ਬੱਖੰ ਮਹਾ ਤੇਜ ਤੱਤੇ ॥੪੨॥
53.t: mile ha'th ba'kha(n) mahaa tej ta'te ||42||
53.e: Absorbed in violent rage, the brave warriors are engaged in war. The heroes with utmost enthusiasm are catching hold the waists of opponents in order to throw them down.42.

53.g: ਝਮੀ ਤੇਜ ਤੇਗੰ ਸੁ ਰੋਸੰ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੰ ॥
53.t: jhamee tej tega(n) su rosa(n) prahaara(n) ||

53.g: ਰੁਲੇ ਰੁੰਡ ਮੁੰਡੰ ਉਠੀ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਝਾਰੰ ॥
53.t: rule ru(n)dd mu(n)dda(n) uThee sasatr jhaara(n) ||
53.e: The sharp swords glisten and are struck with great rage. Somewhere the trunks and heads are rolling in dust and with the collision of weapons, the fire-sparks arise.
Somewhere the warriors are shouting and somewhere the blood is emerging out of the wounds. It appears that Indira and Britrasura are engaged in war 43.

53.g: ਮਹਾਂ ਜੁੱਧ ਮੱਚਿਯੰ ਮਹਾਂ ਸੂਰ ਗਾਜੇ ॥
53.t: mahaa(n) ju'dh ma'chiya(n) mahaa(n) soor gaaje ||

53.g: ਆਪੋ ਆਪ ਮੈਂ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਸੋਂ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਬਾਜੇ ॥
53.t: aapo aap mai(n) sasatr so(n) sasatr baaje ||
53.e: The terrible war is in progress in which the great heroes are thundering. The weapons collide with the confronting weapons.

53.g: ਉਠੇ ਝਾਰ ਸਾਂਗੰ ਮਚੇ ਲੋਹ ਕ੍ਰੋਹੰ ॥
53.t: auThe jhaar saa(n)ga(n) mache loh kroha(n) ||

53.e: The sparks of fire came out of the striking spears and in violent rage, the steel reigns supreme; it seems that good persons, looking impressive, are playing Holi.44.
RASAAVAL STANZA
All the fighters engaged in war against their enemies, ultimately fell as martyrs.
All those who have run away from the battlefield, they all feel ashamed at the end. 45.
The armours of the bodies are broken and the shields have fallen from the hands.
Somewhere there are helmets scattered in the battlefield and somewhere the groups of warriors have fallen.46.
Somewhere the faces with whiskers have fallen, somewhere only weapons are lying.
Somewhere there are scabbards and swords and somewhere there are only few lying in the field.47.
Holding their winsome whiskers, the proud warriors are somewhere engaged in fighting.
Somewhere the weapons are being struck with great knocking on the shield, a great commotion has arisen (in the field). 48
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

53.g: ਖੁਲੇ ਖੱਗ ਖੂਨੀ ਮਹਾਂ ਬੀਰ ਖੇਤੰ ॥
53.t: khule kha'g khoonee mahaa(n) beer kheta(n) ||

53.e: The brave warriors are moving in the battlefield with naked swords, smeared with blood, evil spirits, ghosts, fiends and goblins are dancing.

53.g: ਬਜੇ ਡੰਗ ਡਉਰੂ ਉਠੇ ਨਾਦ ਸੰਖੰ ॥
53.t: baje dda(n)g ddauroo uThe naadh sa(n)kha(n) ||

53.g: ਮਨੋ ਮੱਲ ਜੁੱਟੇ ਮਹਾਂ ਹੱਥ ਬੰਖੰ ॥੪੯॥
53.t: mano ma'l ju'Te mahaa(n) ha'th ba(n)kha(n) ||49||
53.e: The tabor and small drum resound and the sound of conches arises. It appears that the wrestlers, holding with their hands the waists of their opponents are trying to throw them down.49.
CHHAPAI STANZA

53.g: ਜਿਨ ਸੂਰਨ ਸੰਗ੍ਰਾਮ ਸਬਲ ਸਾਮੁਹਿ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਮੰਡਿਓ ॥
53.t: jin sooran sa(n)graam sabal saamuh havai ma(n)ddio ||
53.e: Those warriors who had begun the war confronted their opponents with great strength.

53.g: ਤਿਨ ਸੁਭਟਨ ਤੇ ਏਕ ਕਾਲ ਕੋਊ ਜੀਅਤ ਨ ਛੱਡਿਓ ॥
53.t: tin subhaTan te ek kaal kouoo jeeat na chha'ddio ||
53.e: Out of those warriors the KAL had not left anyone alive.

53.g: ਸਬ ਖੱਤ੍ਰੀ ਖੱਗ ਖੰਡ ਖੇਤ ਭੂ ਮੰਡਪ ਆਹੁੱਟੇ ॥
53.t: sab kha'tree kha'g kha(n)dd khet bhoo ma(n)ddap aahu'Te ||
53.e: All the warriors had gathered in the battlefield holding their swords.

53.g: ਸਾਰ ਧਾਰ ਧਰ ਧੂਮ ਮੁਕਤ ਬੰਧਨ ਤੇ ਛੱੁਟੇ ॥
53.t: saar dhaar dhar dhoom mukat ba(n)dhan te chha'uTe ||
53.e: Enduring the smokeless fire of the steel-edge, they have saved themselves from the bondages.

53.g: ਹ੍ਵੈ ਟੂਕ ਟੂਕ ਜੱੁਝੈ ਸਬੈ ਪਾਵ ਨ ਪਾਛੈ ਡਾਰੀਅੰ ॥
53.t: havai Took Took ja'ujhai sabai paav na paachhai ddaareea(n) ||
53.e: They have all been chopped and fallen as martyrs and none of them hath retraced his steps.

53.g: ਜੈਕਾਰ ਅਪਾਰ ਸੁਧਾਰ ਹੁਅੰ ਬਾਸਿਵ ਲੋਕ ਸਿਧਾਰੀਅੰ ॥੫੦॥
53.t: jaikaar apaar sudhaar hua(n) baasiv lok sidhaareea(n) ||50||
53.e: Those who have gone like this to the abode of Indra, they are hailed with utmost reverence in the world. 50.
CHAUPAI
Suchlike horrible war blazed and the brave warriors left for their (heavenly) abode.
Upto which limit should I describe that war? I cannot describe it with my own understanding.51.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

53.g: ਲਵੀ ਸਰਬ ਜੀਤੇ ਕੁਸੀ ਸਰਬ ਹਾਰੇ ॥
53.t: lavee sarab jeete kusee sarab haare ||

53.g: ਬਚੇ ਜੇ ਬਲੀ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਸਿਧਾਰੇ ॥
53.t: bache je balee praan lai ke sidhaare ||
53.e: (The descendants of Lava) have all been victorious and the (descendants of Kusha) were all defeated. The descendants of Kusha who remained alive, saved themselves by fleeing away.

53.g: ਚਤੁਰ ਬੇਦ ਪਠਿਯੰ ਕੀ੍ਯੋ ਕਾਸਿ ਬਾਸੰ ॥
53.t: chatur bedh paThiya(n) keeyo kaas baasa(n) ||

53.g: ਘਨੇ ਬਰਖ ਕੀਨੇ ਤਹਾਂ ਹੀ ਨਿਵਾਸੰ ॥੫੨॥
53.t: ghane barakh keene tahaa(n) hee nivaasa(n) ||52||
53.e: They went to Kashi and real all the four Vedas. They lived there for many years.52.

53.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਲਵੀ ਕੁਸ਼ੀ ਜੁੱਧ ਬਰਨਨੰ ਨਾਮ ਤ੍ਰਿਤੀਆ ਧਿਆਇ ਸਮਾਪਤ ਮਸਤੁ ਸੁਭ ਮਸਤੁ ॥੩॥ਅਫਜੂ॥੧੮੯॥
53.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the lavee kushee ju'dh baranana(n) naam tirateeaa dhiaai samaapat masat subh masat ||3||afajoo||189||
53.e: End of the Third Chapter of BACHITTAR NATAK entitled The Description of the War of the Descendants of LAVA KUSHA.3.189.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

53.g: ਜਿਨੈ ਬੇਦ ਪਠਿਓ ਸੁ ਬੇਦੀ ਕਹਾਏ ॥
53.t: jinai bedh paThio su bedhee kahaae ||

53.g: ਤਿਨੈ ਧਰਮ ਕੇ ਕਰਮ ਨੀਕੇ ਚਲਾਏ ॥
53.t: tinai dharam ke karam neeke chalaae ||
53.e: Those who studied the Vedas, called Vedis (Bedis), they absorbed themselves in good acts of righteousness.

53.g: ਆਪੋ ਆਪ ਮੋ ਬੈਰ ਭਾਵੰ ਬਿਸਾਰੰ ॥੧॥
53.t: aapo aap mo bair bhaava(n) bisaara(n) ||1||
53.e: The Sodhi king of Madra Desha (Punjab) sent letters to them, entreating them to forget the past enmities.1.

53.g: ਨ੍ਰਿਪੰ ਮੁਕਲਿਅੰ ਦੂਤ ਸੋ ਕਾਸਿ ਆਯੰ ॥
53.t: nirapa(n) mukalia(n) dhoot so kaas aaya(n) ||

53.e: The messengers sent by the king came to Kashi and gave the message to all the Bedis.

53.g: ਸਬੈ ਬੇਦ ਪਾਠੀ ਚਲੇ ਮੱਦ੍ਰ ਦੇਸੰ ॥
53.t: sabai bedh paaThee chale ma'dhr dhesa(n) ||

53.g: ਪ੍ਰਣਾਮੰ ਕੀਯੋ ਆਨ ਕੈ ਕੈ ਨਰੇਸੰ ॥੨॥
53.t: pranaama(n) keeyo aan kai kai naresa(n) ||2||
53.e: All the reciters of the Vedas came to Madra Desha and made obeisance to the king.2.

53.g: ਧੁਨੰ ਬੇਦ ਕੀ ਭੂਪ ਤਾਂ ਤੇ ਕਰਾਈ ॥
53.t: dhuna(n) bedh kee bhoop taa(n) te karaiee ||

53.g: ਸਬੈ ਪਾਸ ਬੈਠੇ ਸਭਾ ਬੀਚ ਭਾਈ ॥
53.t: sabai paas baiThe sabhaa beech bhaiee ||
53.e: The king caused them to recite the Vedas in the traditional manner and all the brethren (both Sodhis and Pelis) sat tohether.

53.g: ਪੜ੍ਹੇ ਸਾਮ ਬੇਦੰ ਜੁਜਰ ਬੇਦ ਕੱਥੰ ॥
53.t: paRhe saam bedha(n) jujar bedh ka'tha(n) ||

53.g: ਰਿਗੰ ਬੇਦ ਪਠਿਯੰ ਕਰੇ ਭਾਵ ਹੱਥੰ ॥੩॥
53.t: riga(n) bedh paThiya(n) kare bhaav ha'tha(n) ||3||
53.e: Saam-Veda, Yajur-Veda and Rig-Ved were recited, the essence of the sayings was imbibed (by the king and his clan).3.
RASAAVAL STANZA
The sin-remover Atharva-Veda was recited.
The king was highly pleased and bequeathed his kingdom to Bedis.4.

54.e: He himself adopted the sin-destroyer Vanaprastha Ashrama.
He put on the garb of a sage (rishi) and gave his kingdom to the reciter (Amrit Rai)5.
The people tried to the king to do so, but, he had abandoned all sorrows.
And leaving his wealth and property, absorbed himself in divine love.6.
ARIL

54.g: ਬੇਦੀ ਭਏ ਪ੍ਰਸੰਨ ਰਾਜ ਕਹ ਪਾਇ ਕੈ ॥
54.t: bedhee bhe prasa(n)n raaj keh pai kai ||

54.g: ਦੇਤ ਭਯੋ ਬਰਦਾਨ ਹੀਐ ਹੁਲਸਾਇ ਕੈ ॥
54.t: dhet bhayo baradhaan heeaai hulasai kai ||
54.e: Having been bestowed the kingdom, the Bedis were very much pleased. With happy heart, he predicted this boon:

54.g: ਜਬ ਨਾਨਕ ਕਲਿ ਮੈ ਹਮ ਆਨ ਕਹਾਇਹੈਂ ॥
54.t: jab naanak kal mai ham aan kahaihai(n) ||

54.g: ਹੋ ਜਗਤ ਪੂਜ ਕਰਿ ਤੋਹਿ ਪਰਮ ਪਦ ਪਾਇਹੈਂ ॥੭॥
54.t: ho jagat pooj kar toh param padh paihai(n) ||7||
54.e: “When in the Iron age, I shall be called Nanak, you will attain the Supreme State and be worshipped by the world.”7.
DOHRA

54.g: ਲਵੀ ਰਾਜ ਦੇ ਬਨ ਗਏ ਬੇਦੀਅਨ ਕੀਨੋ ਰਾਜ ॥
54.t: lavee raaj dhe ban ge bedheean keeno raaj ||
54.e: The descendants of Lava, after handing over the kingdom, went to the forest, and the Bedis (descendants of Kusha) began to rule.

54.g: ਭਾਂਤਿ ਭਾਂਤਿ ਤਿਨਿ ਭੋਗੀਯੰ ਭੂਅ ਕਾ ਸਕਲ ਸਮਾਜ ॥੮॥
54.t: bhaa(n)t bhaa(n)t tin bhogeeya(n) bhooa kaa sakal samaaj ||8||
54.e: They enjoyed all comforts of the earth in various ways.8.
CHAUPAI

54.g: ਚਤੁਰ ਬੇਦ ਸੁਨਿ ਭੂਅ ਕੋ ਦੀਆ ॥
54.t: chatur bedh sun bhooa ko dheeaa ||
54.e: “O Sodhi king! You have listened to the recitation of three Vedas, and while listening to the fourth, you gave away your kingdom.
“When I shall have taken three births"
"You will be made the Guru in the fourth birth.”9.
That (Sodhi) king left for the forest,

54.g: ਇਤ ਇਨ ਰਾਜ ਕਰਤ ਸੁਖ ਪਾਯੋ ॥
54.t: eit in raaj karat sukh paayo ||
54.e: and this (Bedi) king absorbed himself in royal pleasures.
To what extent, I should narrate the story?
It is feared that this granth will become voluminous.10.

54.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਬੇਦ ਪਾਠ ਭੇਟ ਰਾਜ ਚਤੁਰਥ ਧਿਆਇ ਸਮਾਪਤ ਮਸਤੁ ਸੁਭ ਮਸਤੁ ॥੪॥ਅਫਜੂ॥੧੯੯॥
54.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the bedh paaTh bheT raaj chaturath dhiaai samaapat masat subh masat ||4||afajoo||199||
54.e: End of the Fourth Chapter of BACHITTAR NATAK entitled “The Recitation of the Vedas and the Offering of Kingdom”.4.
NARAAJ STANZA
There arose again quarrels and enmities, there was none to defuse the situation.
In due course of time it actually happened that the Bedi caln lost its kingdom.1.
DOHRA

54.g: ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਕਰਤ ਭਏ ਸੂਦ੍ਰ ਬ੍ਰਿਤਿ ਛਤ੍ਰੀ ਬੈਸਨ ਕਰਮ ॥
54.t: bipr karat bhe soodhr birat chhatree baisan karam ||
54.e: The Vaishyas acted like Shudras and Kshatriyas like Vaishyas.

54.g: ਬੈਸ ਕਰਤ ਭਏ ਛਤ੍ਰਿ ਬ੍ਰਿਤਿ ਸੂਦ੍ਰ ਸੁ ਦਿਜ ਕੋ ਧਰਮ ॥੨॥
54.t: bais karat bhe chhatr birat soodhr su dhij ko dharam ||2||
54.e: The Vaishyas acted like Kshatriyas and Shudras like Brahmins.2.
CHAUPAI

54.g: ਬੀਸ ਗਾਵ ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਰਹਿ ਗਏ ॥
54.t: bees gaav tin ke reh ge ||

54.e: Only twenty villages were left with the Bedis, where they became agriculturists.
A long time passed like this till the birth of Nanak.3.
DOHRA

54.g: ਤਿਨ ਬੇਦੀਅਨ ਕੀ ਕੁਲ ਬਿਖੈ ਪ੍ਰਗਟੇ ਨਾਨਕ ਰਾਇ ॥
54.t: tin bedheean kee kul bikhai pragaTe naanak rai ||
54.e: Nanak Rai took birth in the Bedi clan.

54.g: ਸਭ ਸਿੱਖਨ ਕੋ ਸੁਖ ਦਏ ਜਹ ਤਹ ਭਏ ਸਹਾਇ ॥੪॥
54.t: sabh si'khan ko sukh dhe jeh teh bhe sahai ||4||
54.e: He brought comfort to all his disciples and helped them at all times.4.
CHAUPAI

54.g: ਤਿਨ ਇਹ ਕਲ ਮੋ ਧਰਮੁ ਚਲਾਯੋ ॥
54.t: tin ieh kal mo dharam chalaayo ||

54.e: Guru Nanak spread Dharma in the Iron age and put the seekers on the path.

54.g: ਜੋ ਤਾਂ ਕੇ ਮਾਰਗ ਮਹਿ ਆਏ ॥
54.t: jo taa(n) ke maarag meh aae ||

54.e: Those who followed the path propagated by him, were never harmed by the vices.5.

54.g: ਜੇ ਜੇ ਪੰਥ ਤਵਨ ਕੇ ਪਰੇ ॥
54.t: je je pa(n)th tavan ke pare ||

54.g: ਪਾਪ ਤਾਪ ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਹਰੇ ॥
54.t: paap taap tin ke prabh hare ||
54.e: All those who came within his fold, they were absolved of all their sins and troubles,

55.g: ਜਾਲ ਕਾਲ ਕੇ ਬੀਚ ਨ ਆਏ ॥੬॥
55.t: jaal kaal ke beech na aae ||6||
55.e: Their sorrows, their wants were vanished and even their transmigration came to and end.6.

55.g: ਧਰਮ ਪ੍ਰਚੁਰ ਇਹ ਜਗ ਮੋ ਕਰਾ ॥
55.t: dharam prachur ieh jag mo karaa ||
55.e: Nanak transformed himself to Angad and spread Dharma in the world.
He was called Amar Das in the next transformation, a lamp was lit from the lamp.7.
When the opportune time came for the boon, then the Guru was called Ram Das.
The old boon was bestowed upon him, when Amar Das departed for the heavens.8.
Sri Nanak was recognized in Angad, and Angad in Amar Das.
Amar Das was called Ram Das, only the saints know it and the fools did not.9.
The people on the whole considered them as separate ones, but there were few who recognized them as one and the same.

55.g: ਜਿਨ ਜਾਨਾ ਤਿਨ ਹੀ ਸਿਧ ਪਾਈ ॥
55.t: jin jaanaa tin hee sidh paiee ||

55.g: ਬਿਨ ਸਮਝੇ ਸਿਧ ਹਾਥਿ ਨ ਆਈ ॥੧੦॥
55.t: bin samajhe sidh haath na aaiee ||10||
55.e: Those who recognized them as One, they were successful on the spiritual plane. Without recognition there was no success.10.
When Ramdas merged in the Lord, the Guruship was bestowed upon Arjan.
When Arjan left for the abode of the Lord, Hargobind was seated on this throne.11.
When Hargobind left for the abode of the Lord, Har rai was seated in his place.
Har Krishan (the next Guru) was his son, after him, Tegh Bahadur became the Guru.12.

55.g: ਤਿਲਕ ਜੰਞੂ ਰਾਖਾ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਤਾ ਕਾ ॥
55.t: tilak ja(n)n(j)oo raakhaa prabh taa kaa ||
55.e: He protected the forehead mark (tilak) and sacred thread (of the Hindus),
which marked a great event in this age of Kaljug (era of sin).
For the sake of Saints,

55.g: ਸੀਸੁ ਦੀਆ ਪਰੁ ਸੀ ਨ ਉਚਰੀ ॥੧੩॥
55.t: sees dheeaa par see na ucharee ||13||
55.e: He laid down His head without even a sign of pain.
For the sake of Dharma (righteousness),

55.g: ਸੀਸੁ ਦੀਆ ਪਰ ਸਿਰਰੁ ਨ ਦੀਆ ॥
55.t: sees dheeaa par sirar na dheeaa ||
55.e: He sacrificed Himself. He laid down His head, remaining uncompromising in His principles.
The performance of miracles and malpractices...
... is condemned by the Saints of the Lord. (Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Jee refused to show a miracle to avoid the death sentence).
DOHRA

55.g: ਠੀਕਰ ਫੋਰਿ ਦਿਲੀਸ ਸਿਰਿ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਪੁਰਿ ਕੀਯਾ ਪਯਾਨ ॥
55.t: Theekar for dhilees sir prabh pur keeyaa payaan ||
55.e: Breaking the potsherd of his body head of the king of Delhi (Aurangzeb), He left for the abode of the Lord.

55.g: ਤੇਗ ਬਹਾਦਰ ਸੀ ਕ੍ਰਿਆ ਕਰੀ ਨ ਕਿਨਹੂੰ ਆਨ ॥੧੫॥
55.t: teg bahaadhar see kriaa karee na kinahoo(n) aan ||15||
55.e: None could perform such a feat as that of Tegh Bahadur.15.

55.g: ਤੇਗ ਬਹਾਦਰ ਕੇ ਚਲਤ ਭਯੋ ਜਗਤ ਕੋ ਸੋਕ ॥
55.t: teg bahaadhar ke chalat bhayo jagat ko sok ||
55.e: The whole world bemoaned the departure of Tegh Bahadur.

55.g: ਹੈ ਹੈ ਹੈ ਸਭ ਜਗ ਭਯੋ ਜੈ ਜੈ ਜੈ ਸੁਰ ਲੋਕ ॥੧੬॥
55.t: hai hai hai sabh jag bhayo jai jai jai sur lok ||16||
55.e: While the world Iamented, the gods hailed his arrival in heavens.16.

55.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹੀ ਬਰਨਨੰ ਨਾਮ ਪੰਚਮੋ ਧਿਆਇ ਸਮਾਪਤ ਮਸਤ ਸੁਭ ਮਸਤੁ ॥੫॥ਅਫਜੂ॥੨੧੫॥
55.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the paatashaahee baranana(n) naam pa(n)chamo dhiaai samaapat masat subh masat ||5||afajoo||215||
55.e: End of the Fifth Chapter of BACHTTAR NATAK entitled ‘The Description of the Spiritual Kings (Preceptors).5.
CHAUPAI
Now I relate my own story as to how I was brought here,

55.g: ਤਪ ਸਾਧਤ ਜਿਹ ਬਿਧਿ ਮੁਹਿ ਆਨੋ ॥
55.t: tap saadhat jeh bidh muh aano ||
55.e: while I was absorbed in deep meditation.
The site was where Hemkunt mountain is.
The site was the mountain named Hemkunt, with seven peaks, and looks very impressive.1.
That mountain is called Sapt Shring, the seven-peaked mountain.
This is where the Pandavas practiced Yoga.
There, I performed self-discipline and rigorous meditation.
I was absorbed in deep meditation on the Primal Power, the Supreme Destroyer, Kal. 2.

55.g: ਦ੍ਵੈ ਤੇ ਏਕ ਰੂਪ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਗਯੋ ॥
55.t: dhavai te ek roop havai gayo ||
55.e: I became One with the Omnipotent Lord.
My parents also meditated for union with the Incomprehensible Lord.
And they performed many types of worship and meditation for union. 3.

55.g: ਤਿਨ ਜੋ ਕਰੀ ਅਲਖ ਕੀ ਸੇਵਾ ॥
55.t: tin jo karee alakh kee sevaa ||
55.e: The service that they rendered the Incomprehensible Lord,
caused the pleasure of the Supreme Guru.

55.g: ਤਿਨ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਜਬ ਆਇਸ ਮੁਹਿ ਦੀਆ ॥
55.t: tin prabh jab aais muh dheeaa ||

55.g: ਤਬ ਹਮ ਜਨਮ ਕਲੂ ਮਹਿ ਲੀਆ ॥੪॥
55.t: tab ham janam kaloo meh leeaa ||4||
55.e: I was born in this Age of Darkness. 4.

55.g: ਚਿਤ ਨ ਭਯੋ ਹਮਰੋ ਆਵਨ ਕਹ ॥
55.t: chit na bhayo hamaro aavan keh ||
55.e: I had no desire to come,

55.g: ਚੁਭੀ ਰਹੀ ਸ੍ਰੁਤਿ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਚਰਨਨ ਮਹ ॥
55.t: chubhee rahee srut prabh charanan meh ||
55.e: I was totally absorbed in devotion at the Holy feet of the Lord.

55.g: ਜਿਉ ਤਿਉ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਹਮ ਕੋ ਸਮਝਾਯੋ ॥
55.t: jiau tiau prabh ham ko samajhaayo ||
55.e: But the Lord made me understand His Will.

55.g: ਇਮ ਕਹਿ ਕੈ ਇਹ ਲੋਕਿ ਪਠਾਯੋ ॥੫॥
55.t: eim keh kai ieh lok paThaayo ||5||
55.e: Convincing me this way, he sent me to this world. 5.

55.g: ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਾਚ ਇਸ ਕੀਟ ਪ੍ਰਤਿ ॥
55.t: akaal purakh baach is keeT prat ||
55.e: The Words of the Non-temporal Lord to this insect:
CHAUPAI
When I created the world in the beginning, I created the ignominious and dreadful Daityas.

55.g: ਤੇ ਭੁਜ ਬਲ ਬਵਰੇ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਗਏ ॥
55.t: te bhuj bal bavare havai ge ||

55.e: Who became mad with power and abandoned the worship of Supreme Purusha.6.

55.g: ਤੇ ਹਮ ਤਮਕਿ ਤਨਕ ਮੋ ਖਾਪੇ ॥
55.t: te ham tamak tanak mo khaape ||

55.e: I destroyed them in no time and created gods in their place.
They were also absorbed in the worship of power and called themselves Omnipotent.7.

56.e: Mahadeo (Shiva) was called Achyuta (blotless), Vishnu considered himself the Supreme.

56.g: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨ ਕਿਨਹੂੰ ਜਾਨਾ ॥੮॥
56.t: prabh ko prabhoo na kinahoo(n) jaanaa ||8||
56.e: Brahma called himself Para Brahman, none could comprehend the Lord.8.
Then I created eight Sakshis in order to give evidence of my Entity.

56.g: ਹਮ ਬਿਨ ਅਵਰੁ ਨ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਦੂਜਾ ॥੯॥
56.t: ham bin avar na Thaakur dhoojaa ||9||
56.e: But they considered themselves all in all and asked the people to worship them.9.

56.g: ਪਰਮ ਤੱਤ ਕੋ ਜਿਨ ਨ ਪਛਾਨਾ ॥
56.t: param ta't ko jin na pachhaanaa ||

56.g: ਤਿਨ ਕਰਿ ਈਸਰ ਤਿਨ ਕਹੁ ਮਾਨਾ ॥
56.t: tin kar ieesar tin kahu maanaa ||
56.e: Those who did not comprehend the Lord, they were considered as Ishvara.
Several people worshipped the sun and the moon and several others worshipped Fire and Ait.10.
Several of them considered God as stone and several others bathed considering the Lordship of Water.
Considering Dharmaraja as the Supreme representative of Dharma, several bore fear of him in their actions. 11.
All those whom God established for the revelation of His Supremacy, they themselves were called Supreme.

56.g: ਤਾ ਕੀ ਬਾਤ ਬਿਸਰ ਜਾਤੀ ਭੀ ॥
56.t: taa kee baat bisar jaatee bhee ||

56.e: They forgot the Lord in their race for supremacy. 12

56.g: ਜਬ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੋ ਨ ਤਿਨੈ ਪਹਿਚਾਨਾ ॥
56.t: jab prabh ko na tinai pahichaanaa ||

56.e: When they did not comprehend the Lord, then I established human beings in their place.

56.g: ਤੇ ਭੀ ਬਸਿ ਮਮਤਾ ਹੁਇ ਗਏ ॥
56.t: te bhee bas mamataa hui ge ||

56.e: They also were overpowered by ‘mineness’ and exhibited the Lord in statues.13.

56.g: ਤਿਨ ਭੀ ਪਰਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਨਹੀ ਪਾਏ ॥
56.t: tin bhee param purakh nahee paae ||
56.e: Then I created Siddhas and sadhs, who also could not realize the Lord.

56.g: ਜੇ ਕੋਈ ਹੋਤ ਭਯੋ ਜਗਿ ਸਿਆਨਾ ॥
56.t: je koiee hot bhayo jag siaanaa ||

56.e: On whomsoever wisdom dawned, he started his own path. 14.
None could realise the Supreme Lord, but instead spread strife, enmity and ego.

56.g: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੈ ਪੰਥ ਨ ਕੋਊ ਚਲੈ ॥੧੫॥
56.t: prabh kai pa(n)th na kouoo chalai ||15||
56.e: The tree and the leaves began to burn, because of the inner fire.None followed the path of the Lord.15.

56.g: ਜਿਨਿ ਜਿਨਿ ਤਨਿਕ ਸਿੱਧ ਕੋ ਪਾਯੋ ॥
56.t: jin jin tanik si'dh ko paayo ||

56.e: Whosoever attained a little spiritual power, he started his own path.
None could comprehend the Lord, but instead became mad with ‘I-ness’.16.
Nobody recognized the Supreme Essence, but was entangled within himself.
All the great rishis (sages), who were then created, produced their own Smritis.17.

56.g: ਤਿਨਿ ਤਿਨਿ ਕ੍ਰਿਆ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਕੀ ਤਿਆਗੀ ॥
56.t: tin tin kriaa braham kee tiaagee ||
56.e: All those who became followers of these smritis, they abandoned the path of the Lord.

56.g: ਸੋ ਸਿੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਨ ਕੇ ਰਾਹ ਨ ਆਯੋ ॥੧੮॥
56.t: so si(n)mritan ke raeh na aayo ||18||
56.e: Those who devoted themselves to the Feet of the Lord, they did not adopt the path of the Smritis.18.
Brahma composed all the four Vedas, all the people followed the injunctions contained in them.

56.g: ਜਿਨ ਕੀ ਲਿਵ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਨਨ ਲਾਗੀ ॥
56.t: jin kee liv har charanan laagee ||

56.e: Those who were devoted to the Feet of the Lord, they abandoned the Vedas.19.

57.e: Those who abandoned the path of the Vedas and Katebs, they became the devotees of the Lord.

57.g: ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਗੂੜ ਮੱਤ ਜੇ ਚਲਹੀ ॥
57.t: tin ke gooR ma't je chalahee ||

57.e: Whosoever follows their path, he crushes various types of sufferings.20.

57.g: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੇ ਸੰਗਿ ਨ ਛੋਡਤ ਨੇਹ ॥
57.t: prabh ke sa(n)g na chhoddat neh ||
57.e: Those who consider the castes illusory, they do not abandon the love of the Lord.

57.g: ਤੇ ਤੇ ਪਰਮ ਪੁਰੀ ਕਹ ਜਾਹੀ ॥
57.t: te te param puree keh jaahee ||

57.g: ਤਿਨ ਹਰਿ ਸਿਉ ਅੰਤਰੁ ਕਛੁ ਨਾਹੀਂ ॥੨੧॥
57.t: tin har siau a(n)tar kachh naahee(n) ||21||
57.e: When they leave the world, they go to the abode of the Lord, and there is no difference between them and the Lord.21.

57.g: ਜੇ ਜੇ ਜੀਯ ਜਾਤਨ ਤੇ ਡਰੈ ॥
57.t: je je jeey jaatan te ddarai ||

57.g: ਪਰਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਤਜਿ ਤਿਨ ਮਗ ਪਰੈ ॥
57.t: param purakh taj tin mag parai ||
57.e: Those who fear the castes and follow their path, abandoning the Supreme Lord.

57.g: ਤੇ ਤੇ ਨਰਕ ਕੁੰਡ ਮੋ ਪਰਹੀ ॥
57.t: te te narak ku(n)dd mo parahee ||

57.g: ਬਾਰ ਬਾਰ ਜਗ ਮੋ ਬਪੁ ਧਰਹੀ ॥੨੨॥
57.t: baar baar jag mo bap dharahee ||22||
57.e: They fall into hell and transmigrate again and again.22.
Then I created Dutt, who also started his own path.

57.g: ਕਰ ਮੋ ਨਖ ਸਿਰ ਜਟਾਂ ਸਵਾਰੀ ॥
57.t: kar mo nakh sir jaTaa(n) savaaree ||

57.g: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੀ ਕ੍ਰਿਆ ਨ ਕਛੂ ਬਿਚਾਰੀ ॥੨੩॥
57.t: prabh kee kriaa na kachhoo bichaaree ||23||
57.e: His followers have long nails on their hands and matted hair on their heads . They did not understand the ways of the Lord.23
Then I created Gorakh, who made great kings his disciples.

57.g: ਹਰਿ ਕੀ ਪ੍ਰਤਿ ਰੀਤਿ ਨ ਬਿਚਾਰੀ ॥੨੪॥
57.t: har kee prat reet na bichaaree ||24||
57.e: His disciples wear rings in their ears and do not know the love of the lord.24.
Then I created Ramanand, who adopted the path of Bairagi.

57.g: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੀ ਕ੍ਰਿਆ ਨ ਕਛੂ ਬਿਚਾਰੀ ॥੨੫॥
57.t: prabh kee kriaa na kachhoo bichaaree ||25||
57.e: Around his neck he wore necklace of wooden beads and did not comprehend the ways of the Lord.25.
All the great Purushas created by me started their own paths.
Then I created Muhammed, who was made the master of Arabia.26.
He started a religion and circumcised all the kings.
He caused all to utter his name and did not give True Name of the Lord with firmness to anyone.27.
Everyone placed his own interest first and foremost and did not comprehend the Supreme Brahman.

57.g: ਇਮ ਕਹਿ ਕੈ ਇਹ ਲੋਕ ਪਠਾਯੋ ॥੨੮॥
57.t: eim keh kai ieh lok paThaayo ||28||
57.e: When I was busy in the austere devotion, the Lord called me and sent me to this world with the following words.28.
The Word of the Non-Temporal Lord:
CHAUPAI
I have adopted you as my son and hath created you for the propagation of the path (Panth).
“You go therefore for the spread of Dharma (righteousness) and cause people to retrace their steps from evil actions”.29.
The World of the Poet: DOHRA

57.g: ਠਾਢ ਭਯੋ ਮੈ ਜੋਰਿ ਕਰ ਬਚਨ ਕਹਾ ਸਿਰ ਨਿਆਇ ॥
57.t: Thaadd bhayo mai jor kar bachan kahaa sir niaai ||
57.e: I stood up with folded hands and bowing down my head, I said:

57.g: ਪੰਥ ਚਲੈ ਤਬ ਜਗਤ ਮੈ ਜਬ ਤੁਮ ਕਰਹੁ ਸਹਾਇ ॥੩੦॥
57.t: pa(n)th chalai tab jagat mai jab tum karahu sahai ||30||
57.e: “The path (Panth) shall prevail only in the world, with THY ASSISTANCE.”30.
CHAUPAI
For this reason the Lord sent me.

57.g: ਤਬ ਮੈ ਜਗਤ ਜਨਮ ਧਰਿ ਆਯੋ ॥
57.t: tab mai jagat janam dhar aayo ||
57.e: And then I was born into this world.

57.g: ਜਿਮ ਤਿਨ ਕਹੀ ਤਿਨੈ ਤਿਮ ਕਹਿਹੋਂ ॥
57.t: jim tin kahee tinai tim kahiho(n) ||
57.e: Whatever the Lord said, I am repeating the same unto you.

58.g: ਅਉਰ ਕਿਸੂ ਤੇ ਬੈਰ ਨ ਗਹਿਹੋਂ ॥੩੧॥
58.t: aaur kisoo te bair na gahiho(n) ||31||
58.e: I do not bear enmity towards anyone. 31.
Whosoever shall call me the Lord,

58.g: ਤੇ ਸਭ ਨਰਕ ਕੁੰਡ ਮਹਿ ਪਰਿਹੈਂ ॥
58.t: te sabh narak ku(n)dd meh parihai(n) ||
58.e: shall all fall into the pits of hell.

58.g: ਮੋ ਕੌ ਦਾਸ ਤਵਨ ਕਾ ਜਾਨੋ ॥
58.t: mo kau dhaas tavan kaa jaano ||
58.e: Consider me the servant of the Transcendent Lord.

58.g: ਯਾ ਮੈ ਭੇਦ ਨ ਰੰਚ ਪਛਾਨੋ ॥੩੨॥
58.t: yaa mai bhedh na ra(n)ch pachhaano ||32||
58.e: Do not think of any difference between me and Him. 32.

58.g: ਮੈ ਹੋ ਪਰਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਕੋ ਦਾਸਾ ॥
58.t: mai ho param purakh ko dhaasaa ||
58.e: I am the servant of the Supreme Being.
I have come to see the spectacle of the world.

58.g: ਜੋ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਜਗਤਿ ਕਹਾ ਸੋ ਕਹਿਹੋਂ ॥
58.t: jo prabh jagat kahaa so kahiho(n) ||
58.e: Whatever the Lord of the world said,

58.g: ਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਲੋਕ ਤੇ ਮੋਨ ਨ ਰਹਿਹੋਂ ॥੩੩॥
58.t: mirat lok te mon na rahiho(n) ||33||
58.e: I say the same unto you, I cannot remain silent in this abode of death. 33.
NAARAAJ CHHAND
I say only that which the Lord hath said, I do not yield to anyone else.
I do not feel pleased with any particular garb, I sow the seed of God’s Name.34.
I do not worship stones, nor I have any liking for a particular guise.
I sing the Name (of the Lord),
I sing infinite Names (of the Lord), and meet the Supreme Purusha.35.
I do not wear matted hair on my head, nor do I put rings in my ears.
I do not pay attention to anyone else, all my actions are at the bidding of the Lord.36.
I recite only the Name of the Lord, which is useful at all places.
I do not meditate on anyone else, nor do I seek assistance from any other quarter.37.
I recite infinite Names and attain the Supreme light.
I do not meditate on anyone else, nor do I repeat the Name of anyone else.38.
I am absorbed only in the Name of the Lord, and honour none else.
By meditating on the Supreme, I am absolved of infinite sins.39.
I am absorbed only in His Sight, and do not attend to any other charitable action.
By uttering only His Name, I am absolved of infinite sorrows.40.
CHAUPAI
Those who meditated on Your Name,

58.g: ਦੂਖ ਪਾਪ ਤਿਹ ਨਿਕਟ ਨ ਆਇਆ ॥
58.t: dhookh paap teh nikaT na aaiaa ||
58.e: no sorrows and sins came near them.

58.g: ਜੇ ਜੇ ਅਉਰ ਧਿਆਨ ਕੋ ਧਰਹੀਂ ॥
58.t: je je aaur dhiaan ko dharahee(n) ||
58.e: Those who meditated on any other
died in futile discussions and quarrels in the end. ||41||

58.g: ਹਮ ਇਹ ਕਾਜ ਜਗਤ ਮੋ ਆਏ ॥
58.t: ham ieh kaaj jagat mo aae ||
58.e: I have come into the world for this purpose.
The Divine Guru sent me to propagate the righteous way of life.
In this way, You asked me to spread the righteous path,
and vanquish evil tyrants. ||42||
I have taken birth for this purpose.

58.g: ਸਮਝ ਲੇਹੁ ਸਾਧੂ ਸਭ ਮਨ ਮੰ ॥
58.t: samajh leh saadhoo sabh man ma(n) ||
58.e: The saints should understand this in their minds.
To protect the saints and spread the true path.
To destroy all of the evil tyrants at their root. ||43||
Those earlier incarnations that manifested,
Caused others to meditate only on their own names.
Not one of them struck down the enemies of God,

58.g: ਧਰਮ ਕਰਨ ਕੋ ਰਾਹੁ ਨ ਡਾਰਾ ॥੪੪॥
58.t: dharam karan ko raahu na ddaaraa ||44||
58.e: Nor proselytized about the righteous path. ||44||
The earlier prophets, ascetics, and wise-ones

58.g: ਮੈ ਮੈ ਕਰਤ ਜਗਤ ਤੇ ਗਏ ॥
58.t: mai mai karat jagat te ge ||
58.e: All were filled with ego and left this world.
Not one recognized the Supreme Being.

58.g: ਕਰਮ ਧਰਮ ਕੋ ਕਛੂ ਨ ਜਾਨਾ ॥੪੫॥
58.t: karam dharam ko kachhoo na jaanaa ||45||
58.e: Nor did they care for righteous deeds. ||45||
Hope in any other is worthless.
There is only one hope that should dwell in your mind.
Hope in others will never be fruitful.

58.g: ਵਾ ਕੀ ਆਸ ਧਰੋਂ ਮਨ ਮਾਹੀ ॥੪੬॥
58.t: vaa kee aas dharo(n) man maahee ||46||
58.e: This is why, only one hope should dwell within your mind. ||46||
DOHRA

58.g: ਕੋਈ ਪੜ੍ਹਤ ਕੁਰਾਨ ਕੋ ਕੋਈ ਪੜ੍ਹਤ ਪੁਰਾਨ ॥
58.t: koiee paRhat kuraan ko koiee paRhat puraan ||
58.e: Someone studies the Quran and someone studies the Puranas.

58.g: ਕਾਲ ਨ ਸਕਤ ਬਚਾਇ ਕੈ ਫੋਕਟ ਧਰਮ ਨਿਦਾਨ ॥੪੭॥
58.t: kaal na sakat bachai kai fokaT dharam nidhaan ||47||
58.e: Mere reading cannot save one from death. Therefore such works are vain and do not help at the time of death.47.
CHAUPAI
Millions of people recite the Quran and many study Puranas witout understanding the crux.

58.g: ਅੰਤ ਕਾਲ ਕੋਈ ਕਾਮ ਨ ਆਵਾ ॥
58.t: a(n)t kaal koiee kaam na aavaa ||

58.e: It will be of no use at the time of death and none will be saved.48.

58.g: ਕਿਉ ਨ ਜਪੋ ਤਾ ਕੋ ਤੁਮ ਭਾਈ ॥
58.t: kiau na japo taa ko tum bhaiee ||

59.e: O Brother! Why do you not meditate on Him, who will help you at the time of death?

59.g: ਇਨ ਤੇ ਸਰਤ ਨ ਕੋਈ ਕਰਮਾ ॥੪੯॥
59.t: ein te sarat na koiee karamaa ||49||
59.e: Consider the vain religions as illusory, because they do not serve our purpose (of life).49.
For this reason the Lord created me and sent me in this world, telling me the secret.

59.g: ਜੋ ਤਿਨ ਕਹਾ ਸੁ ਸਭਨ ਉਚਰੋਂ ॥
59.t: jo tin kahaa su sabhan ucharo(n) ||

59.g: ਡਿੰਭ ਵਿੰਭ ਕਛੁ ਨੈਕ ਨ ਕਰੋਂ ॥੫੦॥
59.t: ddi(n)bh vi(n)bh kachh naik na karo(n) ||50||
59.e: Whatever He told me, I say unto you, there is not even a little heresay in it.50.
RASAAVAL STANZA
I neither wear matted hair on the head nor bedeck myself with ear-rings.
I meditate on the Name of the Lord, which helps me in all my errands.51.
Neither I close my eyes, nor exhibit heresy.
Nor perform evil actions, nor cause others to call me a person in disguise. 52.
CHAUPAI

59.g: ਜੇ ਜੇ ਭੇਖ ਸੁ ਤਨ ਮੈਂ ਧਾਰੈ ॥
59.t: je je bhekh su tan mai(n) dhaarai ||

59.g: ਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਜਨ ਕਛੁ ਕੈ ਨ ਬਿਚਾਰੈ ॥
59.t: te prabh jan kachh kai na bichaarai ||
59.e: Those persons who adopt different guises are never liked by the men of God.

59.g: ਸਮਝ ਲੇਹੁ ਸਭ ਜਨ ਮਨ ਮਾਹੀ ॥
59.t: samajh leh sabh jan man maahee ||

59.e: All of you may understanding this that God is absent form all these guises.53.

59.g: ਜੇ ਜੇ ਕਰਮ ਕਰਿ ਡਿੰਭ ਦਿਖਾਹੀਂ ॥
59.t: je je karam kar ddi(n)bh dhikhaahee(n) ||

59.g: ਤਿਨ ਪਰ ਲੋਗਨ ਮੋ ਗਤਿ ਨਾਹੀਂ ॥
59.t: tin par logan mo gat naahee(n) ||
59.e: Those who exhibit various garbs through various actions, they never get release in the next world.
While alive, their worldly desires may be fulfilled and the king may be pleased on seeing their mimicry.54.

59.g: ਖੋਜ ਫਿਰੈ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਕੋ ਕਾਹੀ ॥
59.t: khoj firai sabh hee ko kaahee ||
59.e: The Lord-God is not present in such mimics, even all the places be searched by all.

59.g: ਅਪਨੋ ਮਨੁ ਕਰ ਮੋ ਜਿਹ ਆਨਾ ॥
59.t: apano man kar mo jeh aanaa ||

59.e: Only those who controlled their minds, recognized the Supreme Brahman.55.
DOHRA

59.g: ਭੇਖ ਦਿਖਾਇ ਜਗਤ ਕੋ ਲੋਗਨ ਕੋ ਬਸਿ ਕੀਨ ॥
59.t: bhekh dhikhai jagat ko logan ko bas keen ||
59.e: Those who exhibit various guises in the world and win people on their side.

59.g: ਅੰਤਿ ਕਾਲ ਕਾਤੀ ਕਟਿਓ ਬਾਸੁ ਨਰਕ ਮੋ ਲੀਨ ॥੫੬॥
59.t: a(n)t kaal kaatee kaTio baas narak mo leen ||56||
59.e: They will reside in hell, when the sword of death chops them. 56.
CHUPAI

59.g: ਜੇ ਜੇ ਜਗ ਕੋ ਡਿੰਭ ਦਿਖਾਵੈ ॥
59.t: je je jag ko ddi(n)bh dhikhaavai ||

59.e: Those who exhibit different guises, find disciples and enjoy great comforts.
Those who their nostrils and perform prostrations, their religious discipline is vain and useless.57.
All the followers of the futile path, fall into hell from within.

59.g: ਜੋ ਮਨੁ ਜੀਤ ਸਕਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਾਹੂ ॥੫੮॥
59.t: jo man jeet sakaa nahee(n) kaahoo ||58||
59.e: They cannot go to heavens with the movement of the hands, because they could not control their minds in any way. 58.
The Words of the Poet: DOHRA

59.g: ਜੋ ਨਿਜ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਮੋ ਸੋ ਕਹਾ ਸੋ ਕਹਿਹੋਂ ਜਗ ਮਾਹਿ ॥
59.t: jo nij prabh mo so kahaa so kahiho(n) jag maeh ||
59.e: Whatever my Lord said to me, I say the same in the world.

59.g: ਜੋ ਤਿਹ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੋ ਧਿਆਇ ਹੈ ਅੰਤ ਸੁਰਗ ਕੋ ਜਾਹਿ ॥੫੯॥
59.t: jo teh prabh ko dhiaai hai a(n)t surag ko jaeh ||59||
59.e: Those who have meditated on the Lord, ultimately go to heaven.59.
DOHRA

59.g: ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਨ ਦੁਇ ਏਕ ਹੈ ਬਿਬ ਬਿਚਾਰ ਕਛੁ ਨਾਹਿ ॥
59.t: har har jan dhui ek hai bib bichaar kachh naeh ||
59.e: The Lord and His devotees are one, there is no difference between them.

59.g: ਜਲ ਤੇ ਉਪਜ ਤਰੰਗ ਜਿਉ ਜਲ ਹੀ ਬਿਖੈ ਸਮਾਹਿ ॥੬੦॥
59.t: jal te upaj tara(n)g jiau jal hee bikhai samaeh ||60||
59.e: Just as the wave of water, arising in water, merges in water.60.
CHAUPAI

60.e: Those who quarrel in ego, they are far removed from the Lord.
O men of God! Understand this that the Lord doth not reside in Vedas and katebs. 61.
He, who exhibits heresy in closing his eyes, attains the state of blindness.

60.g: ਆਂਖਿ ਮੀਚ ਮਗ ਸੂਝ ਨ ਜਾਈ ॥
60.t: aa(n)kh meech mag soojh na jaiee ||

60.e: By closing the eyes one cannot know the path, how can then, O brother! He meet the Infinite Lord?62.

60.g: ਬਹੁ ਬਿਸਥਾਰ ਕਹ ਲਉ ਕੋਈ ਕਹੈ ॥
60.t: bahu bisathaar keh lau koiee kahai ||

60.e: To what extent, can the details be given? When one understands, he feels tired.

60.g: ਤਦਪਿ ਗਨਤ ਤਿਹ ਪਰਤ ਸੁ ਤੋਟਾ ॥੬੩॥
60.t: tadhap ganat teh parat su toTaa ||63||
60.e: If one is blessed with millions of tongues, even then he feels them short in number, (while singing the Praises of the Lord)63.
DOHRA

60.g: ਜਬ ਆਇਸੁ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੋ ਭਯੋ ਜਨਮੁ ਧਰਾ ਜਗ ਆਇ ॥
60.t: jab aais prabh ko bhayo janam dharaa jag aai ||
60.e: When the Lord Willed, I was born on this earth.

60.g: ਅਬ ਮੈ ਕਥਾ ਸੰਛੇਪ ਤੇ ਸਬਹੂੰ ਕਹਤ ਸੁਨਾਇ ॥੬੪॥
60.t: ab mai kathaa sa(n)chhep te sabahoo(n) kahat sunai ||64||
60.e: Now I shall narrate briefly my own story.64.

60.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਮਮ ਆਗਿਆ ਕਾਲ ਜਗ ਪ੍ਰਵੇਸ ਕਰਨ ਨਾਮ ਖਸਟਮੋ ਧਿਆਇ ਸਮਾਪਤ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭ ਮਸਤੁ ॥੬॥ਅਫਜੂ॥੨੭੯॥
60.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the mam aagiaa kaal jag praves karan naam khasaTamo dhiaai samaapat sat subh masat ||6||afajoo||279||
60.e: End of the Sixth Chapter of BACHITTAR NATAK entitled The Command of Supreme KAL to Me for Coming into the World.6.279.
HERE BEGINS THE DESCRIPTION OF THE BIRTH OF THE POET.
CHAUPAI
My father (Guru Tegh Bahadur) proceeded towards the east.
He bathed at several places of pilgrimage.
When he went to Triveni (Prayag),
he passed his days in acts of charity ||1||
I was conceived there.
I took birth at Patna City.

60.g: ਮੱਦ੍ਰ ਦੇਸ ਹਮ ਕੋ ਲੇ ਆਏ ॥
60.t: ma'dhr dhes ham ko le aae ||
60.e: When I was brought to Punjab,
I was nurtured by various nurses. ||2||
I was given physical protection in various ways.
And I was given various types of education.

60.g: ਜਬ ਹਮ ਧਰਮ ਕਰਮ ਮੋ ਆਏ ॥
60.t: jab ham dharam karam mo aae ||
60.e: When I began to understand the righteous path,
my father departed for his heavenly abode ||3||

60.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਕਬਿ ਜਨਮ ਕਥਨੰ ਨਾਮ ਸਪਤਮੋ ਧਿਆਇ ਸਮਾਪਤ ਮਸਤੁ ਸੁਭ ਮਸਤੁ ॥੭॥ਅਫਜੂ॥੨੮੨॥
60.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the kab janam kathana(n) naam sapatamo dhiaai samaapat masat subh masat ||7||afajoo||282||
60.e: End of the Seventh Chapter of BACHITTTAR NATAK entitled Description of the Poet.7.282
Here begins the Description of the Magnificence of Authority:
CHAUPAI

60.g: ਰਾਜ ਸਾਜ ਹਮ ਪਰ ਜਬ ਆਯੋ ॥
60.t: raaj saaj ham par jab aayo ||

60.e: When I obtained the position of responsibility, I performed the religious acts to the best of my ability.
I went hunting various kinds of animals in the forest and killed bears, nilgais (blue bulls) and elks.1.

60.g: ਦੇਸ ਚਾਲ ਹਮ ਤੇ ਪੁਨਿ ਭਈ ॥
60.t: dhes chaal ham te pun bhiee ||

60.e: Then I left my home and went to place named Paonta.
I enjoyed my stay on the banks of Kalindri (Yamuna) and saw amusement of various kind2.

60.g: ਤਹ ਕੇ ਸਿੰਘ ਘਨੇ ਚੁਨਿ ਮਾਰੇ ॥
60.t: teh ke si(n)gh ghane chun maare ||

60.e: There I killed many lions, nilgais and bears.

60.g: ਲੋਹ ਪਰਾ ਹਮ ਸੋ ਬਿਨੁ ਕਾਜਾ ॥੩॥
60.t: loh paraa ham so bin kaajaa ||3||
60.e: On this the king Fateh Shah become angry and fought with me without any reason.3.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

60.g: ਪੰਚੋ ਬੀਰ ਬੰਕੇ ਪ੍ਰਿਥੀ ਪਾਇ ਰੋਪੇ ॥
60.t: pa(n)cho beer ba(n)ke pirathee pai rope ||
60.e: There Sri Shah (Sango Shah) become enraged and all the five warriors stood firmly in the battlefield.
Including the tenacious Jit Mal and the desparate hero Gulab, whose faces were red with ire, in the field.4.
The persistent Mahari Chand and Ganga Ram, who had defeated lot of forces.
Lal Chand was red with anger, who had shattered pride of several lion-like heroes.5.
Maharu got enraged and with frightening expression killed brave Khans in the battlefield.

60.g: ਕੀਯੋ ਦ੍ਰੋਣ ਕੀ ਜਿਉ ਮਹਾ ਜੱੁਧ ਸੱੁਧੰ ॥੬॥
60.t: keeyo dhron kee jiau mahaa ja'udh sa'udha(n) ||6||
60.e: The godly Daya Ram, filled with great ire, fought very heroically in the field like Dronacharya.6.
Kirpal in rage, rushed with his mace and struck it on the head of the tenacious Hayaat Khan.

60.g: ਉੱਠੀ ਛਿੱਛ ਇੱਛੰ ਕਢਾ ਮੇਝ ਜੋਰੰ ॥
60.t: au'Thee chhi'chh i'chha(n) kaddaa mejh jora(n) ||

60.e: With all his might, he caused the marrow flow out of his head, which splashed like the butter spattering out of the pitcher of butter broken by lord Krishan.7.
Then Nand Chand, in fierce rage, wielding his sword struck it with force.
But it broke. Then he drew his dagger and the tenacious warrior saved the honour of the Sodhi clan.8.

60.g: ਛਕਿਓ ਛੋਭ ਛੱਤ੍ਰੀ ਕਰਯੋ ਜੱੁਧ ਸੱੁਧੰ ॥
60.t: chhakio chhobh chha'tree karayo ja'udh sa'udha(n) ||
60.e: Then the Maternal uncle Kirpal, in great ire, manifested the war-feats like a true Kshatriya.

60.g: ਸਹੇ ਦੇਹ ਆਪੰ ਮਹਾਂ ਬੀਰ ਬਾਣੰ ॥
60.t: sahe dheh aapa(n) mahaa(n) beer baana(n) ||

60.e: The great hero was struck by an arrow, but he caused the brave Khan to fall from the saddle.9.
Sahib Chand, the valiant Kshatriya, killed a bloody Khan of Khorasan.

61.g: ਤਹਾਂ ਬੀਰ ਬੰਕੇ ਭਲੀ ਭਾਂਤਿ ਮਾਰੇ ॥
61.t: tahaa(n) beer ba(n)ke bhalee bhaa(n)t maare ||

61.g: ਬਚੇ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਸਿਪਾਹੀ ਸਿਧਾਰੇ ॥੧੦॥
61.t: bache praan lai ke sipaahee sidhaare ||10||
61.e: He slew several graceful warriors, with full force  the soldiers who survived, fled away in order to save their lives.10.

61.g: ਘਨੇ ਖੇਤ ਮੋ ਖਾਨ ਖੂਨੀ ਲਤਾਰੇ ॥
61.t: ghane khet mo khaan khoonee lataare ||
61.e: There (Sango) Shah exhibited his acts of bravery in the battlefield and trampled under feet many bloody Khans.

61.g: ਮ੍ਰਿਗਾ ਝੁੰਡ ਮੱਧਿਯੰ ਮਨੋ ਸਿੰਘ ਰਾਜੈ ॥੧੧॥
61.t: miragaa jhu(n)dd ma'dhiya(n) mano si(n)gh raajai ||11||
61.e: Gopal, the king of Guleria, stood firmly in the field and roared like a lion amidst a herd of deers.11.

61.g: ਤਹਾਂ ਏਕ ਬੀਰੰ ਹਰੀ ਚੰਦ ਕੋਪ੍ਯੋ ॥
61.t: tahaa(n) ek beera(n) haree cha(n)dh kopayo ||

61.g: ਭਲੀ ਭਾਂਤਿ ਸੋ ਖੇਤ ਮੋ ਪਾਵ ਰੋਪ੍ਯੋ ॥
61.t: bhalee bhaa(n)t so khet mo paav ropayo ||
61.e: There in great fury, a warrior Hari Chand, very skillfully took position in the battlefield.

61.g: ਮਹਾ ਕ੍ਰੋਧ ਕੈ ਤੀਰ ਤੀਖੇ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੇ ॥
61.t: mahaa krodh kai teer teekhe prahaare ||

61.g: ਲਗੈ ਜੌਨ ਕੇ ਤਾਹਿ ਪਾਰੈ ਪਧਾਰੇ ॥੧੨॥
61.t: lagai jauan ke taeh paarai padhaare ||12||
61.e: He discharged sharp arrows in great rage and whosoever was struck, left for the other world.12.
RASAAVAL STANZA
Hari Chand (Handooria) in great fury, killed significant heroes.
He shot skillfully a volley of arrows and killed a lot of forces.13.
He was absorbed in dreadful feat of arms.
Armed warriors were being killed and great kings were falling on the ground.14.
Then Jit Mal aimed and struck Hari Chand down to the ground with his spear.15.
The warriors struck with arrows became red with blood.
Their horses feel and they left for heavens.16.
BHUJANG PRAYAAAT STANZA

61.g: ਪਰੀ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਧਾਰੰ ਉਠੀ ਝਾਲ ਅੱਗੰ ॥
61.t: paree sasatr dhaara(n) uThee jhaal a'ga(n) ||
61.e: In the hands of blood-thirsty Khans, there were the Khorasan swords, whose sharp edges flashed like fire.

61.g: ਗਿਰੇ ਬਾਜ ਤਾਜੀ ਲਗੇ ਧੀਰ ਧੱਕੇ ॥੧੭॥
61.t: gire baaj taajee lage dheer dha'ke ||17||
61.e: The bows shooing out volleys of arrows twanged, the splendid horses fell because of the heavy blows.17.

61.g: ਦੁਹੂੰ ਓਰ ਤੇ ਬੀਰ ਬੰਕੇ ਬਕਾਰੇ ॥
61.t: dhuhoo(n) or te beer ba(n)ke bakaare ||
61.e: The trumpets sounded and the musical pipes were played, the brave warriors thundered from both sides.
And with their strong arms struck (the enemy), the witches drank blood to their fill and produced dreadful sounds.18.
DOHRA

61.g: ਕਹਾ ਲਗੇ ਬਰਨਨ ਕਰੋਂ ਮਚਿਯੋ ਜੁਧੁ ਅਪਾਰ ॥
61.t: kahaa lage baranan karo(n) machiyo judh apaar ||
61.e: How far should I describe the great battle?

61.g: ਜੇ ਲੱੁਝੇ ਜੁੱਝੇ ਸਬੈ ਭੱਜੇ ਸੂਰ ਹਜਾਰ ॥੧੯॥
61.t: je la'ujhe ju'jhe sabai bha'je soor hajaar ||19||
61.e: Those fought attained martyrdom, thousands fled away. 19.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA
The hill-chief spurred his horse and fled, the warriors went away without discharging their arrows.

61.g: ਭਜੇ ਸੰਗਿ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਸੁ ਸਾਰੀ ਸਿਪਾਹੰ ॥੨੦॥
61.t: bhaje sa(n)g lai ke su saaree sipaaha(n) ||20||
61.e: The chiefs of Jaswal and Dadhwal, who were fighting (in the field), left with all their soldiers.20.
The Raja of Chandel was perplexed, when the tenacious Hari Chand caught hold of the spear in his hand.

61.g: ਕਰਿਓ ਸੁਆਮਿ ਧਰਮੰ ਮਹਾ ਰੋਸ ਰੁੱਝਿਯੰ ॥
61.t: kario suaam dharama(n) mahaa ros ru'jhiya(n) ||
61.e: He was filled with great fury, fulfilling his duty as a general

61.g: ਗਿਰਿਓ ਟੂਕ ਟੂਕ ਹ੍ਵੈ ਇਸੋ ਸੂਰ ਜੁੱਝਿਯੰ ॥੨੧॥
61.t: girio Took Took havai iso soor ju'jhiya(n) ||21||
61.e: Those who came in front of him, were cut into pieces and fell (in the field).21.

62.g: ਤਹਾ ਖਾਨ ਨੈਜਾਬਤੋ ਆਨ ਕੈ ਕੈ ॥
62.t: tahaa khaan naijaabato aan kai kai ||

62.g: ਹਨਿਓ ਸਾਹ ਸੰਗ੍ਰਾਮ ਕੌ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਲੈ ਕੈ ॥
62.t: hanio saeh sa(n)graam kau sasatr lai kai ||
62.e: Then Najabat Khan came forward and struck Sango Shah with his weapons.

62.g: ਕਿਤੈ ਖਾਨ ਬਾਨੀਨ ਹੂੰ ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ਝਾਰੇ ॥
62.t: kitai khaan baaneen hoo(n) asatr jhaare ||

62.e: Several skillful Khans fell on him with their arms and sent Shah Sangram to heaven.22.
DOHRA

62.g: ਮਾਰਿ ਨਜਾਬਤ ਖਾਨ ਕੋ ਸੰਗੋ ਜੁਝੈ ਜੁਝਾਰ ॥
62.t: maar najaabat khaan ko sa(n)go jujhai jujhaar ||
62.e: The brave warrior Sago Shah fell down after killing Najbat Khan.

62.g: ਹਾ ਹਾ ਇਹ ਲੋਕੈ ਭਇਓ ਸੁਰਗ ਲੋਕ ਜੈਕਾਰ ॥੨੩॥
62.t: haa haa ieh lokai bhio surag lok jaikaar ||23||
62.e: There were lamentations in his world and rejoicing in heaven.23.
BHUJANG STANZA
When this lowly person saw Shah Sangram falling (while fighting bravely) he held aloft his bow and arrows.

62.g: ਡਸਿਯੋ ਸਤ੍ਰੁ ਕੋ ਜਾਨੁ ਸ੍ਯਾਮੰ ਭੁਜੰਗੰ ॥੨੪॥
62.t: ddasiyo satr ko jaan sayaama(n) bhuja(n)ga(n) ||24||
62.e: He, fixing his gaze on a Khan, shot an arrow, which stung the enemy like a black cobra, who (the Khan) fell down.24.

62.g: ਗਿਰਿਯੋ ਭੂਮ ਸੋ ਬਾਣ ਦੂਜੋ ਸੰਭਾਰਯੋ ॥
62.t: giriyo bhoom so baan dhoojo sa(n)bhaarayo ||

62.g: ਮੁਖੰ ਭੀਖਨੰ ਖਾਨ ਕੇ ਤਾਨਿ ਮਾਰਯੋ ॥
62.t: mukha(n) bheekhana(n) khaan ke taan maarayo ||
62.e: He drew out another arrow and aimed and shot it on the face of Bhikhan Khan.

62.g: ਭਜਿਯੋ ਖਾਨ ਖੂਨੀ ਰਹਿਯੋ ਖੇਤ ਤਾਜੀ ॥
62.t: bhajiyo khaan khoonee rahiyo khet taajee ||

62.g: ਤਜੇ ਪ੍ਰਾਣ ਤੀਜੇ ਲਗੇ ਬਾਣ ਬਾਜੀ ॥੨੫॥
62.t: taje praan teeje lage baan baajee ||25||
62.e: The bloody Khan fled away leaving his horse in the field, who was killed with the third arrow.25.

62.g: ਗਹੇ ਬਾਣ ਕਾਮਾਨ ਭੇ ਐਂਚ ਮਾਰੇ ॥
62.t: gahe baan kaamaan bhe aai(n)ch maare ||
62.e: After regaining consciousness from the swoon, Hari Chand shot his arrows with unerring aim.

62.g: ਲਗੇ ਅੰਗ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਰਹੇ ਨ ਸੰਭਾਰੰ ॥
62.t: lage a(n)g jaa ke rahe na sa(n)bhaara(n) ||

62.e: Whosoever was struck, fell down unconscious, and leaving his body, went to the heavenly abode.26.

62.g: ਦੁਯੰ ਬਾਨ ਖੈਂਚੇ ਇਕੰ ਬਾਰ ਮਾਰੇ ॥
62.t: dhuya(n) baan khai(n)che ika(n) baar maare ||

62.e: He aimed and shot two arrows at the same time and did not care for the selection of his target.

62.g: ਜਿਸੈ ਬਾਨ ਲਾਗੈ ਰਹੈ ਨ ਸੰਭਾਰੰ ॥
62.t: jisai baan laagai rahai na sa(n)bhaara(n) ||

62.g: ਤਨੰ ਬੇਧਿ ਕੈ ਤਾਹਿ ਪਾਰੰ ਸਿਧਾਰੰ ॥੨੭॥
62.t: tana(n) bedh kai taeh paara(n) sidhaara(n) ||27||
62.e: Whosoever was struck and pierced by his arrow, went straight to the other world.27.

62.g: ਸਬੈ ਸ੍ਵਾਮਿ ਧਰਮੰ ਸੁ ਬੀਰੰ ਸੰਭਾਰੇ ॥
62.t: sabai savaiaam dharama(n) su beera(n) sa(n)bhaare ||

62.e: The warriors remained true to their duty in the field, the witches and ghosts drank blood to their fill and raised shrill voices.

62.g: ਹਸੇ ਬੀਰ ਬੈਤਾਲ ਔ ਸੁੱਧ ਸਿੱਧੰ ॥
62.t: hase beer baitaal aau su'dh si'dha(n) ||

62.e: The Birs (heroic spirits), Baitals (ghosts) and Siddhs (adepts) laughed, the witches were talking and huge kites were flying (for meat).28.
Hari Chand, filled with rage, drew out his bow, he aimed and shot his arrow, which struck my horse.

62.g: ਦੁਤੀਯ ਤਾਕ ਕੈ ਤੀਰ ਮੋ ਕੌ ਚਲਾਯੰ ॥
62.t: dhuteey taak kai teer mo kau chalaaya(n) ||

62.g: ਰਖਿਓ ਦਈਵ ਮੈ ਕਾਨਿ ਛ੍ਵੈ ਕੈ ਸਿਧਾਯੰ ॥੨੯॥
62.t: rakhio dhieev mai kaan chhavai kai sidhaaya(n) ||29||
62.e: He aimed and shot the second arrow towards me, the Lord protected me, his arrow only grazed my ear. 29.

62.g: ਤ੍ਰਿਤੀਯ ਬਾਣ ਮਾਰਿਯੋ ਸੁ ਪੇਟੀ ਮਝਾਰੰ ॥
62.t: tirateey baan maariyo su peTee majhaara(n) ||

62.e: His third arrow penetrated deep into the buckle of my waist-belt.

62.g: ਚੁਭੀ ਚਿੰਚ ਚਰਮੰ ਕਛੂ ਘਾਇ ਨ ਆਯੰ ॥
62.t: chubhee chi(n)ch charama(n) kachhoo ghai na aaya(n) ||

62.e: Its edge touched the body, but did not caused a wound, the Lord saved his servent.30.
RASAAVAL STANZA
When the edge of the arrow touched my body, it kindled my resentment.
I took the bow in my hand and aimed and shot the arrow.31.
All the warriors fled, when a volley of arrow was showered.
Then I aimed the arrow on a warrior and killed him.32.
Hari Chand was killed and his brave soldiers were trampled.

63.e: The chief of Kot Lehar was seized by death.33.
The hill-men fled from the battlefield, all were filled with fear.
I gained victory through the favour of the Eternal Lord (KAL).34.
We returned after victory and sang songs of triumph.
I showered wealth on the warriors, who were full of rejoicings.35.
DOHRA

63.g: ਜੁਧ ਜੀਤ ਆਏ ਜਬੈ ਟਿਕੈ ਨ ਤਿਨ ਪੁਰ ਪਾਂਵ ॥
63.t: judh jeet aae jabai Tikai na tin pur paa(n)v ||
63.e: When I returned after victory, I did not remain at Paonta.

63.g: ਕਾਹਲੂਰ ਮੈ ਬਾਂਧਿਯੋ ਆਨ ਆਨੰਦਪੁਰ ਗਾਂਵ ॥੩੬॥
63.t: kaahaloor mai baa(n)dhiyo aan aana(n)dhapur gaa(n)v ||36||
63.e: I came to Kahlur and established the village Anandpur.36.

63.g: ਜੇ ਜੇ ਨਰ ਤਹ ਨ ਭਿਰੇ ਦੀਨੇ ਨਗਰ ਨਿਕਾਰ ॥
63.t: je je nar teh na bhire dheene nagar nikaar ||
63.e: Those, who did not join the forces, were turned out from the town.

63.g: ਜੇ ਤਿਹ ਠਉਰ ਭਲੇ ਭਿਰੇ ਤਿਨੈ ਕਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਤਿਪਾਰ ॥੩੭॥
63.t: je teh Thaur bhale bhire tinai karee pratipaar ||37||
63.e: And those who fought bravely were patronized by me 37.
CHAUPAI
Many days passed in this way, the saints were protected and the wicked persons were killed.
The tyrants were hanged ultimately killed, they breathed their last like dogs.38.

63.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਭੰਗਾਣੀ ਜੁੱਧ ਬਰਨਨੰ ਨਾਮ ਅਸਟਮੋ ਧਿਆਇ ਸਮਾਪਤ ਮਸਤੁ ਸੁਭ ਮਸਤੁ ॥੮॥ਅਫਜੂ॥੩੨੦॥
63.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the bha(n)gaanee ju'dh baranana(n) naam asaTamo dhiaai samaapat masat subh masat ||8||afajoo||320||
63.e: End of the Eighth Chapter of BACHITTAR NATAK entitled ‘Description of the Battle of Bhangani.’8.320.
Here begins the Description of the Battle of Nadaun:
CHAUPAI
Much time passed in this way, Mian Khan came (from Delhi) to Jammu (for collection of revenue).
He sent Alif Khan to Nadaun, who developed enmity towards Bhim Chand (the Chief of Kahlur).1.
Bhim Chnad called me for assistance and himself went to face (the enemy).

63.g: ਤਿਨ ਕਠ ਗੜ ਨਵਰਸ ਪਰ ਬਾਂਧਯੋ ॥
63.t: tin kaTh gaR navaras par baa(n)dhayo ||

63.e: Alif Khan prepared a wooden fort of the hill of Navras. The hill-chief also prepared their arrows and guns.2.
BHUJANG STANZA

63.g: ਚੜਿਓ ਰਾਮ ਸਿੰਘੰ ਮਹਾ ਤੇਜ ਵੰਦੰ ॥
63.t: chaRio raam si(n)gha(n) mahaa tej va(n)dha(n) ||
63.e: With brave Bhim Chand, there were Raj Singh, illustrious Ram Singh,

63.g: ਚੜੇ ਕ੍ਰੁੱਧ ਕੀਨੇ ਕਰੇ ਸਰਬ ਕਾਜੰ ॥੩॥
63.t: chaRe kru'dh keene kare sarab kaaja(n) ||3||
63.e: And Sukhdev Gaji of Jasrot, were full of fury and managed their affairs with enthusiasm.3.

63.g: ਚਲੇ ਸਿੱਧ ਹੁਐ ਕਾਰ ਰਾਜੰ ਸੁਧਾਰੰ ॥
63.t: chale si'dh huaai kaar raaja(n) sudhaara(n) ||
63.e: There came also the brave Prithi Chand of Dadhwar after having made arrangements regarding the affairs of his state.

63.g: ਹਟਾਏ ਸਬੈ ਮਾਰਿ ਕੈ ਬੀਰ ਬ੍ਰਿੰਦੰ ॥੪॥
63.t: haTaae sabai maar kai beer bira(n)dha(n) ||4||
63.e: Kirpal Chand (of Kanara) arrived with ammunition and drove back and killed many of the warriors (of Bhim Chand).4.

63.g: ਦੁਤੀਯ ਢੋਅ ਢੂਕੇ ਵਹੈ ਮਾਰਿ ਉਤਾਰੀ ॥
63.t: dhuteey ddoa ddooke vahai maar utaaree ||

63.e: When for the second time, the forces of Bhim Chand advanced, they were beaten back downwards to the great sorrow of (the allies of Bhim Chand),

63.g: ਉਤੈ ਵੈ ਖਰੇ ਬੀਰ ਬੰਬੈ ਬਜਾਵੈਂ ॥
63.t: autai vai khare beer ba(n)bai bajaavai(n) ||

63.g: ਤਰੇ ਭੂਪ ਠਾਂਢੇ ਬਡੋ ਸੋਕੁ ਪਾਵੈਂ ॥੫॥
63.t: tare bhoop Thaa(n)dde baddo sok paavai(n) ||5||
63.e: The warriors on the hill sounded trumpets, while the chiefs below were filled with remorse.5.

63.g: ਹਨੂਮਾਨ ਕੇ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਕੋ ਮੁਖ ਜਾਪੰ ॥
63.t: hanoomaan ke ma(n)tr ko mukh jaapa(n) ||
63.e: Then Bhim Chand was filled with great ire and began to recite the incantations of Hanuman.

63.g: ਸਬੈ ਬੀਰ ਬੋਲੈ ਹਮੈ ਭੀ ਬੁਲਾਯੰ ॥
63.t: sabai beer bolai hamai bhee bulaaya(n) ||

63.g: ਤਬੈ ਢੋਅ ਕੈ ਕੈ ਸੁ ਨੀਕੈ ਸਿਧਾਯੰ ॥੬॥
63.t: tabai ddoa kai kai su neekai sidhaaya(n) ||6||
63.e: He called all his warriors and also called me. Then all assembled and advanced for attack.6.

63.g: ਸਬੈ ਕੋਪ ਕੈ ਕੈ ਮਹਾ ਬੀਰ ਢੂਕੈ ॥
63.t: sabai kop kai kai mahaa beer ddookai ||

63.g: ਚਲੇ ਬਾਰਿਬੇ ਬਾਰ ਕੋ ਜਿਉ ਭਭੂਕੈ ॥
63.t: chale baaribe baar ko jiau bhabhookai ||
63.e: All the great warriors marched forward with great ire like a flame over a fence of dry weeds.

63.g: ਉਠਿਓ ਸੈਨ ਲੈ ਸੰਗਿ ਸਾਰੀ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾਲੰ ॥੭॥
63.t: auThio sain lai sa(n)g saaree kirapaala(n) ||7||
63.e: Then on the other side, the valiant Raja Dayal of Bijharwal advanced with Raja Kirpal, along with all his army.7.
MADHUBHAAR STANZA
Kirpal Chand was in great fury. The horses danced.
And the pipes were played which presented a dreadful scene.8.
The warriors foutht and struck their swords.
With rage, they showered volley of arrows.9.
The fighting soldiers fell in the field and breathed their last.
They fell. Like thundering clouds on the earth.10.
RASAVAL STANZA
Kirpal Chand, in great anger, stood firmly in the field.
With his volley of arrows, he killed great warriors.11.
He killed the chief, who lay dead on the ground.

64.g: ਭਲੇ ਸੂਰ ਗਾਜੇ ॥੧੨॥
64.t: bhale soor gaaje ||12||
64.e: The trumpets sounded and the warriors thundered.12.

64.g: ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾਲੰ ਕੱ੍ਰੁਧੰ ॥
64.t: kirapaala(n) ka'rudha(n) ||

64.g: ਕੀਯੋ ਜੁੱਧ ਸੁੱਧੰ ॥
64.t: keeyo ju'dh su'dha(n) ||
64.e: Kirpal Chand, in great fury, made a great fight.

64.g: ਮਹਾਂ ਬੀਰ ਗੱਜੇ ॥
64.t: mahaa(n) beer ga'je ||

64.g: ਮਹਾਂ ਸਾਰ ਬੱਜੇ ॥੧੩॥
64.t: mahaa(n) saar ba'je ||13||
64.e: Great heroes thundered, while using dreadful weapons.13.

64.g: ਕਰਿਯੋ ਜੱੁਧ ਚੰਡੰ ॥
64.t: kariyo ja'udh cha(n)dda(n) ||

64.g: ਸੁਣਿਯੋ ਨਾਵ ਖੰਡੰ ॥
64.t: suniyo naav kha(n)dda(n) ||
64.e: Such a heroic battle was fought that all the people of the world living in nine quarters, knew it.

64.g: ਚਲਿਯੋ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਬਾਹੀ ॥
64.t: chaliyo sasatr baahee ||

64.g: ਰਜੌਤੀ ਨਿਬਾਹੀ ॥੧੪॥
64.t: rajauatee nibaahee ||14||
64.e: His weapons wrought havoc and he exhibited himself as a true rajput. ||14||

64.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
64.t: dhoharaa ||
64.e: DOHRA

64.g: ਕੋਪ ਭਰੇ ਰਾਜਾ ਸਬੈ ਕੀਨੋ ਜੁੱਧ ਉਪਾਇ ॥
64.t: kop bhare raajaa sabai keeno ju'dh upai ||
64.e: All the chiefs of the allies, in great anger, entered the fray.

64.g: ਸੈਨ ਕਟੋਚਨ ਕੀ ਤਬੈ ਘੇਰ ਲਈ ਅਰਰਾਇ ॥੧੫॥
64.t: sain kaTochan kee tabai gher liee ararai ||15||
64.e: And besieged the army of Katoch. 15.

64.g: ਭੁਜੰਗ ਛੰਦ ॥
64.t: bhuja(n)g chha(n)dh ||
64.e: BHUJANG STANZA

64.g: ਚਲੇ ਨਾਂਗਲੂ ਪਾਂਗਲੂ ਵੇਦੜੋਲੰ ॥
64.t: chale naa(n)galoo paa(n)galoo vedhaRola(n) ||

64.g: ਜਸਵਾਰੇ ਗੁਲੇਰੇ ਚਲੇ ਬਾਂਧ ਟੋਲੰ ॥
64.t: jasavaare gulere chale baa(n)dh Tola(n) ||
64.e: The Rajputs of the tribes of Nanglua and Panglu advanced in groups alongwith the soldiers of Jaswar and Guler.

64.g: ਤਹਾਂ ਏਕ ਬਾਜਿਓ ਮਹਾਂ ਬੀਰ ਦਿਆਲੰ ॥
64.t: tahaa(n) ek baajio mahaa(n) beer dhiaala(n) ||

64.g: ਰਖੀ ਲਾਜ ਜੌਨੇ ਸਭੈ ਬਿਝੜਵਾਲੰ ॥੧੬॥
64.t: rakhee laaj jauane sabhai bijhaRavaala(n) ||16||
64.e: The greater warrior Dayal also joined and saved the honour of the people of Bijharwal. 16.

64.g: ਤਵੰ ਕੀਟ ਤੌ ਲੌ ਤੁਫੰਗੰ ਸੰਭਾਰੋ ॥
64.t: tava(n) keeT tau lau tufa(n)ga(n) sa(n)bhaaro ||

64.g: ਹ੍ਰਿਦੈ ਏਕ ਰਾਵੰਤ ਕੇ ਤੱਕਿ ਮਾਰੋ ॥
64.t: hiradhai ek raava(n)t ke ta'k maaro ||
64.e: Then this lowly person (the Guru himself) took up his gun and aimed unerringly at one of the chiefs.

64.g: ਗਿਰਿਓ ਝੂਮ ਭੂਮੈ ਕਰਿਯੋ ਜੁਧ ਸੁੱਧੰ ॥
64.t: girio jhoom bhoomai kariyo judh su'dha(n) ||

64.g: ਤਊ ਮਾਰਿ ਬੋਲਿਯੋ ਮਹਾ ਮਾਨਿ ਕ੍ਰੁੱਧੰ ॥੧੭॥
64.t: tuoo maar boliyo mahaa maan kru'dha(n) ||17||
64.e: He reeled and fell down on the ground in the battlefield, but even then he thundered in anger.17.

64.g: ਤਜਿਯੋ ਤੁਪਕੰ ਬਾਨ ਪਾਨੰ ਸੰਭਾਰੇ ॥
64.t: tajiyo tupaka(n) baan paana(n) sa(n)bhaare ||

64.g: ਚਤੁਰ ਬਾਨਯੰ ਲੈ ਸੁ ਸੱਬਿਯੰ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੇ ॥
64.t: chatur baanaya(n) lai su sa'biya(n) prahaare ||
64.e: I then threw away the gun and took the arrows in my hand, I shot four of them.

64.g: ਤ੍ਰਿਯੋ ਬਾਨ ਲੈ ਬਾਮ ਪਾਨੰ ਚਲਾਏ ॥
64.t: tirayo baan lai baam paana(n) chalaae ||

64.g: ਲਗੇ ਯਾ ਲਗੇ ਨਾ ਕਛੂ ਜਾਨਿ ਪਾਏ ॥੧੮॥
64.t: lage yaa lage naa kachhoo jaan paae ||18||
64.e: Another three I discharged with my left hand, whether they struck anybody, I do not know. 18.

64.g: ਸੁ ਤਉ ਲਉ ਦਈਵ ਜੁਧ ਕੀਨੋ ਉਝਾਰੰ ॥
64.t: s tau lau dhieev judh keeno ujhaara(n) ||

64.g: ਤਿਨੈ ਖੇਦ ਕੈ ਬਾਰਿ ਕੇ ਬੀਚ ਡਾਰੰ ॥
64.t: tinai khedh kai baar ke beech ddaara(n) ||
64.e: Then the Lord brought the end of the fight and the enemy was driven out into the river.

64.g: ਪਰੀ ਮਾਰ ਬੁੰਗੰ ਛੁਟੀ ਬਾਣ ਗੋਲੀ ॥
64.t: paree maar bu(n)ga(n) chhuTee baan golee ||

64.g: ਮਨੋ ਸੂਰ ਬੈਠੇ ਭਲੀ ਖੇਲ ਹੋਲੀ ॥੧੯॥
64.t: mano soor baiThe bhalee khel holee ||19||
64.e: Form the hill the bullets and arrows were showered. It seemed that the sun set down after playing a good holi.19.

64.g: ਗਿਰੇ ਬੀਰ ਭੂਮੰ ਸਰੰ ਸਾਂਗ ਪੇਲੰ ॥
64.t: gire beer bhooma(n) sara(n) saa(n)g pela(n) ||

64.g: ਰੰਗੇ ਸ੍ਰੌਣ ਬਸਤ੍ਰੰ ਮਨੋ ਫਾਗ ਖੇਲੰ ॥
64.t: ra(n)ge srauan basatra(n) mano faag khela(n) ||
64.e: Pierced by arrows and spears, the warriors fell in the battlefield. Their clothes were dyed with blood, it seemed that they played holi.

64.g: ਲੀਯੋ ਜੀਤਿ ਬੈਰੀ ਕੀਆ ਆਨਿ ਡੇਰੰ ॥
64.t: leeyo jeet bairee keeaa aan ddera(n) ||

64.g: ਤੇਊ ਜਾਇ ਪਾਰੰ ਰਹੇ ਬਾਰਿ ਕੇਰੰ ॥੨੦॥
64.t: teuoo jai paara(n) rahe baar kera(n) ||20||
64.e: After conquering the enemy, they came for rest at heir place of encampment, on the other side of the reiver. 20.

64.g: ਭਈ ਰਾਤ੍ਰਿ ਗੁਬਾਰ ਕੇ ਅਰਧ ਜਾਮੰ ॥
64.t: bhiee raatr gubaar ke aradh jaama(n) ||

64.g: ਤਬੈ ਛੋਰਿਗੇ ਬਾਰ ਦੇਵੈ ਦਮਾਮੰ ॥
64.t: tabai chhorige baar dhevai dhamaama(n) ||
64.e: Sometime after midnight they left, while beating the drums.

64.g: ਸਬੈ ਰਾਤ੍ਰਿ ਬੀਤੀ ਉਦਿਓ ਦਿਉਸਰਾਣੰ ॥
64.t: sabai raatr beetee udhio dhiausaraana(n) ||

64.g: ਚਲੇ ਬੀਰ ਚਾਲਾਕ ਖੱਗੰ ਖਿਲਾਣੰ ॥੨੧॥
64.t: chale beer chaalaak kha'ga(n) khilaana(n) ||21||
64.e: When the whole night ended and the sun arose, the warriors outside marched hastily, brandishing their spears.21.

64.g: ਭਜਿਓ ਅਲਫ ਖਾਨੰ ਨ ਖਾਨਾ ਸੰਭਾਰਿਓ ॥
64.t: bhajio alaf khaana(n) na khaanaa sa(n)bhaario ||

64.g: ਭਜੇ ਅਉਰ ਬੀਰੰ ਨ ਧੀਰੰ ਬਿਚਾਰਿਓ ॥
64.t: bhaje aaur beera(n) na dheera(n) bichaario ||
64.e: Alif Khan fled away, leaving back his belongings. All the other warriors fled away and did not stay anywhere.

64.g: ਨਦੀ ਪੈ ਦਿਨੰ ਅਸਟ ਕੀਨੇ ਮੁਕਾਮੰ ॥
64.t: nadhee pai dhina(n) asaT keene mukaama(n) ||

64.g: ਭਲੀ ਭਾਂਤਿ ਦੇਖੇ ਸਬੈ ਰਾਜ ਧਾਮੰ ॥੨੨॥
64.t: bhalee bhaa(n)t dhekhe sabai raaj dhaama(n) ||22||
64.e: I remained there on the bank of the river for eight more days and visited the palaces of all the chiefs.22.

64.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
64.t: chauapiee ||
64.e: CHAUPAI

64.g: ਇਤ ਹਮ ਹੋਇ ਬਿਦਾ ਘਰ ਆਏ ॥
64.t: eit ham hoi bidhaa ghar aae ||

64.g: ਸੁਲਹ ਨਮਿਤ ਵੈ ਉਤਹਿ ਸਿਧਾਏ ॥
64.t: suleh namit vai uteh sidhaae ||
64.e: Then I took leave and came home, they went there to settle the terms of peace.

64.g: ਸੰਧਿ ਇਨੈ ਉਨ ਕੈ ਸੰਗਿ ਕਈ ॥
64.t: sa(n)dh inai un kai sa(n)g kiee ||

64.g: ਹੇਤ ਕਥਾ ਪੂਰਨ ਇਤ ਭਈ ॥੨੩॥
64.t: het kathaa pooran it bhiee ||23||
64.e: Both the parties made and agreement, therefore the story ends here.23.

64.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
64.t: dhoharaa ||
64.e: DOHRA

64.g: ਆਲਸੂਨ ਕਹ ਮਾਰਿ ਕੈ ਇਹ ਦਿਸਿ ਕੀਓ ਪਿਯਾਨ ॥
64.t: aalasoon keh maar kai ieh dhis keeo piyaan ||
64.e: I came to this side after destroying alsun on my way

65.g: ਭਾਤਿ ਅਨੇਕਨ ਕੇ ਕਰੇ ਪੁਰ ਅਨੰਦ ਸੁਖ ਆਨ ॥੨੪॥
65.t: bhaat anekan ke kare pur ana(n)dh sukh aan ||24||
65.e: And enjoyed in various ways after reaching Anandpur.24.

65.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਨਦੌਨ ਜੁੱਧ ਬਰਨਨੰ ਨਾਮ ਨੌਮੋ ਧਿਆਇ ਸਮਾਪਤ ਮਸਤੁ ਸੁਭ ਮਸਤੁ ॥੯॥ਅਫਜੂ॥੩੪੪॥
65.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the nadhauan ju'dh baranana(n) naam nauamo dhiaai samaapat masat subh masat ||9||afajoo||344||
65.e: End of Ninth Chapter of BACHITTAR NATAK entitled ‘Description of the battle of Nadaun.9.344.
CHAUPAI

65.g: ਚੁਨਿ ਚੁਨਿ ਚੋਰ ਸਬੈ ਗਹਿ ਘਾਏ ॥
65.t: chun chun chor sabai geh ghaae ||
65.e: Many years elapsed in this way, all the wicked persons (thieves) were spotted, caught and killed.
Some of them fled away from the city, but came back on account of starvation.1.
Then Dilwar Khan (Governor of Lahore) sent his son against me.
A few hours after nightfall, the Khans assembled and advanced for attack.2

65.g: ਜਬ ਦਲ ਪਾਰ ਨਦੀ ਕੇ ਆਯੋ ॥
65.t: jab dhal paar nadhee ke aayo ||

65.e: When their forces crossed the river, Alam (Singh) came and woke me up.

65.g: ਸੋਰੁ ਪਰਾ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਨਰ ਜਾਗੇ ॥
65.t: sor paraa sabh hee nar jaage ||

65.g: ਗਹਿ ਗਹਿ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਬੀਰ ਰਿਸ ਪਾਗੇ ॥੩॥
65.t: geh geh sasatr beer ris paage ||3||
65.e: There was a great consternation and all the people got up. They took up their arms with valour and zeal.3.

65.g: ਗਹਿ ਗਹਿ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਰਿਸਾਨੇ ਸਬ ਹੀ ॥
65.t: geh geh sasatr risaane sab hee ||
65.e: The discharge of the volleys of shots from guns began immediately. Everyone was in a rage, holding the arms in hand.
They raised various dreadful shouts. The noise was heard on the other side of the river.4.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA
The bugles blew, the trumpets resounded, the great heroes entered the fray, shouting loudly.
From both sides, the arms clattered with force and the horses danced, it seemed that the dreadful goddess Kali thundered in the battlefield.5.
The river appeared like the night of death  the severe chill cramped the soldiers.

65.g: ਇਤੇ ਬੀਰ ਗੱਜੇ ਭਏ ਨਾਦ ਭਾਰੇ ॥
